rics.meaning: China industrial output: New energy bus production. Industrial-sector production data for specific products or sub-sectors.
rics.how_to_use: Track for sector-cycle dynamics. China is the world's largest producer of steel, cement, copper, aluminum, and many other industrial commodities. rics.description: Industrial companies above designated size, profit margin of main business, electrical & electrical industry, year on year, cumulative
rics.meaning: Profit margin of main business for industrial companies above designated size (annual revenue ≥ CNY 20M) in the electrical and electronic industry, reported on a year-on-year cumulative basis. Published monthly by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) as part of the Industrial Enterprise Financial Statistics survey, typically released ~27th of the following month. Covers profit-to-revenue ratios across the broad electrical/electronics manufacturing complex.
rics.how_to_use: Use to gauge pricing power and cost pass-through dynamics in China's electronics sector — margins above 5-6% signal healthy demand; compression below 3% often precedes capacity rationalization. Compare against the PPI for electronic equipment (aCNCNQTYNM) to separate pricing from cost effects. A sustained YoY deterioration of 1+ percentage point tends to lead export-order softening by 1-2 quarters.

rics.description: Industrial companies above designated size, profit margin of main business, heavy mining industry
rics.meaning: Profit margin on main business revenue for industrial companies above designated size (annual revenue >CNY 20M) in the heavy mining sector, published monthly by China's National Bureau of Statistics (NBS). Covers ferrous and non-ferrous mining, coal, and stone quarrying as an aggregate. Released with a ~30-day lag alongside the broader industrial profits dataset.
rics.how_to_use: A margin below 3% in heavy mining signals acute stress — watch for production cuts by smaller private miners and potential credit events in the sector. Compare against steel PPI (aCNCNNFMEM) to assess pass-through: when downstream prices recover but this margin stays compressed, input cost (energy, labor) pressures dominate. Useful as a lead for NBS mining capex surveys.

rics.description: Coal consumption of power generation, 6000 kW & above
rics.meaning: Annual coal consumption at power plants with installed capacity of 6,000 kW and above, published by the NBS in the annual China Energy Statistical Yearbook. Captures the dominant end-use of thermal coal in China, where power generation accounts for roughly 55% of total coal demand (~2.5 billion tonnes/year of the ~4.5 billion tonne total).
rics.how_to_use: Year-on-year changes reflect electricity demand growth and fuel-switching trends (gas, nuclear, renewables displacing coal). A >5% YoY rise in power-sector coal burn typically precedes tightness in thermal coal spot markets and supports Qinhuangdao benchmark prices. Pair with industrial capacity utilization in coal mining (aCNCNKWDNQ) to assess supply-demand balance.

rics.description: Electricity consumption coal mining & washing industry, Hubei Province
rics.meaning: Annual electricity consumed by the coal mining and washing industry in Hubei Province, published by the NBS in provincial energy balance tables. Hubei is a mid-sized coal consumer rather than a major producer (unlike Shanxi or Inner Mongolia), so this series primarily reflects local washing and processing activity rather than raw extraction volume.
rics.how_to_use: Use as a cross-check on coal processing throughput in central China: rising power consumption with flat raw coal output (aCNCNKMHRM) implies higher washing ratios and improved product quality mix. Divergence from Zhejiang's equivalent (aCNCNJYRB) can highlight regional demand shifts in cleaned coal supply chains feeding Yangtze River industrial clusters.

rics.description: Electricity consumption coal mining & washing industry, Zhejiang Province
rics.meaning: Annual electricity consumed by the coal mining and washing industry in Zhejiang Province, published by the NBS in provincial energy statistical tables. Zhejiang has negligible coal mining output, so this series is almost entirely attributable to coal washing and coking plants that process coal transported from northern provinces.
rics.how_to_use: Rising Zhejiang coal-processing power use alongside falling northern mine-mouth prices implies stronger spot coal flows into the industrialised Yangtze Delta. Useful when triangulated with coal port inventory data and the NBS coal mining capacity utilisation rate (aCNCNKWDNQ) to gauge south-bound coal logistics tightness.

rics.description: Electricity used, calcium carbide manufacturing
rics.meaning: Annual electricity consumed by calcium carbide manufacturing firms above designated size in China. Published by NBS as part of the annual industrial energy consumption census, typically released in the first quarter following the reference year. Calcium carbide is an energy-intensive intermediate used in PVC production, acetylene chemistry, and steel desulfurization.
rics.how_to_use: A proxy for PVC and basic chemical output activity — China produces roughly 25-28 million tonnes of calcium carbide per year, accounting for ~70% of global supply. Rising electricity consumption year-on-year signals strong PVC pipeline demand and construction-linked chemical activity. Cross-reference with NBS PVC output data and coal prices (calcium carbide plants are largely coal-powered) to assess margin pressure.

rics.description: Key enterprise electrical steel strip sales volume
rics.subcategory: Electrical Steel Strip Sales — Key Enterprises
rics.meaning: Monthly sales volume of electrical steel strip (silicon steel/grain-oriented and non-oriented) at key Chinese steel enterprises, compiled by the China Iron and Steel Association (CISA). Electrical steel is a premium, capital-intensive product used in transformer cores and EV motor stators; China achieved near-self-sufficiency in grain-oriented grades around 2015.
rics.how_to_use: Electrical steel demand is a direct proxy for power grid investment (State Grid capex cycles) and EV motor production growth — both structural growth areas. A monthly sales run-rate above 800 kt signals robust grid and EV demand. Cross with aCNCNPBMZM (total key-enterprise steel sales) to calculate electrical steel's share; rising share reflects product mix upgrading away from commodity rebar.

rics.description: Key enterprise steel sales
rics.meaning: Monthly aggregate steel sales volume across all product categories at major Chinese steel enterprises tracked by CISA. This is the broadest sales-side steel indicator from China's key producer cohort, covering roughly 60-65% of national crude steel output, published within two weeks of month-end.
rics.how_to_use: The ratio of this series to key-enterprise crude steel production (aCNCNCOSM) yields an implied sell-through rate; below 95% for two consecutive months typically precedes inventory build-up and price weakness. A surprise divergence of >5% from headline NBS crude steel output (aCNPDCRDS) often indicates smaller induction-furnace producers (outside CISA coverage) are running hot.

rics.description: Key enterprises' crude steel output
rics.meaning: Monthly crude steel production at key enterprises surveyed by CISA — China's most timely steel production indicator, typically released 10-15 days before the official NBS figure. The CISA sample (~200 large mills) accounts for approximately 65% of national output and includes Baowu, HBIS, Shagang, Ansteel, and Jianlong.
rics.how_to_use: Use as the leading indicator ahead of the NBS release (aCNPDCRDS). When CISA output runs >5% above year-ago levels for three consecutive months, expect NBS to confirm an output surge and watch iron ore futures (DCE i2509) for price compression. Production above 85 Mt/month nationally (implied by scaling CISA data) is historically associated with margin pressure and government output-cap rhetoric.

rics.description: Key enterprises, steel production
rics.meaning: Monthly total steel production (finished steel, including rolled products) at key CISA-tracked enterprises, distinct from aCNCNCOSM which measures crude steel at the liquid-steel stage. This series captures the downstream transformation step — rolling and forming — providing a picture of finished product supply entering the market.
rics.how_to_use: Compare against aCNCNCOSM to derive an implied crude-to-finished yield; when yields fall (more scrap, rejects), product mix is shifting toward lower-value flat/long products. A finished steel output surge without accompanying sales growth (aCNCNPBMZM) signals inventory accumulation at mills — a bearish signal for near-term prices, especially rebar and HRC.

rics.description: Large-scale steel sales volume of key enterprises
rics.subcategory: Large Section Steel Sales — Key Enterprises
rics.meaning: Monthly sales volume of large-section steel products (heavy H-beams, large angle steel, channel sections) at key CISA enterprises. Large sections are primarily consumed in infrastructure — bridges, port cranes, industrial buildings — and in shipbuilding; demand is less sensitive to property cycles than rebar but highly correlated with fixed-asset investment in transport infrastructure.
rics.how_to_use: When large-section sales outperform total steel sales (aCNCNPBMZM) growth by >3 ppts, it signals infrastructure-led demand is compensating for property weakness — a pattern seen post-2021 as Beijing pivoted to FAI stimulus. Compare with civil steel ship production (aCNCNZGMEM) as another large-section end-use. Monthly volumes above 2 Mt at CISA firms indicate a healthy order book.

rics.description: Other steel sales volume of key enterprises
rics.meaning: Monthly sales volume of the residual 'other steel' category at key CISA enterprises — encompassing semi-finished billets, ingots, specialty alloy bars, and niche grades not separately classified. This catch-all category is volatile month-to-month and can spike when mills sell semi-finished billets into the spot market rather than rolling them internally.
rics.how_to_use: A sharp rise in 'other steel' relative to finished products often signals downstream rolling capacity constraints or downstream demand weakness forcing mills to liquidate semi-finished inventory externally. Cross with billet prices on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE): rising billet prices concurrent with high 'other' sales volumes indicates external rolling mills are absorbing supply at profitable spreads.

rics.description: Sales volume of medium & thick steel strips in key enterprises
rics.subcategory: Medium & Thick Steel Strip Sales — Key Enterprises
rics.meaning: Monthly sales volume of medium and thick steel strip (typically 3–20 mm gauge hot-rolled strip/coil) at key CISA enterprises. This product category feeds pipe mills (oil/gas line pipe, structural tubing), shipbuilding, and heavy machinery — end-markets with distinct cycles from property-driven rebar and wire rod.
rics.how_to_use: Track alongside China's shipbuilding order book (aCNCNZGMEM) and pipeline CAPEX cycles. When medium/thick strip sales grow faster than thin flat products, it indicates strength in industrial and energy-sector demand rather than consumer-linked sectors. Monthly run-rates above 3.5 Mt across CISA firms historically align with active shipbuilding seasons (March–October).

rics.description: Sales volume of small & medium-sized steel in key enterprises
rics.subcategory: Small & Medium Section Steel Sales — Key Enterprises
rics.meaning: Monthly sales of small and medium steel sections (rebar, angle iron, channel steel, I-beams in standard sizes) at key CISA enterprises. This is the most property-sensitive steel product category — rebar alone accounts for ~30% of China's finished steel demand, predominantly going into residential construction reinforcement.
rics.how_to_use: This series is the clearest steel-to-property linkage: when new home starts collapse (as during 2022–2024 deleveraging), small/medium section sales typically fall 10-20% YoY. A recovery above 0% YoY growth in this series is an early signal of property sector stabilisation. Compare monthly against aCNCNPBMZM to calculate mix share — small/medium sections below 35% of total sales confirms structural shift toward infrastructure/industrial flat products.

rics.description: Sales volume of tinplates (belts) of key enterprises
rics.meaning: Monthly sales volume of tinplate and tin-coated steel strip at key CISA enterprises. Tinplate is a premium flat-rolled product with a thin tin coating (1–12 g/m²), primarily used for food and beverage cans, aerosol containers, and battery casings. China's tinplate output (~4 Mt/year) is dominated by Baosteel and Shougang.
rics.how_to_use: Tinplate sales are driven by consumer packaged goods and beverage can demand — relatively defensive versus construction-linked steels. When tinplate sales hold up while rebar sales fall, it confirms the domestic consumer sector is decoupling from property weakness. Watch for shifts to aluminium can substitution, which has eroded tinplate share globally; a multi-month decline in this series warrants cross-checking aluminium can production data.

rics.description: Alumina production
rics.meaning: Monthly national alumina (aluminum oxide, Al₂O₃) production in China, published by the NBS. Alumina is the intermediate product refined from bauxite ore via the Bayer process before being smelted into primary aluminum; China produces ~75 Mt/year (~55% of global supply), with Henan, Shanxi, and Guangxi as the key provinces.
rics.how_to_use: Alumina production is the critical upstream bottleneck for aluminum smelting (aCNCNTPTOM and others): ~2 tonnes of alumina per tonne of aluminum. When national alumina output grows faster than aluminum production, it rebuilds the alumina-aluminum spread and pressures alumina spot prices (currently referenced to API-basis or Australian spot). A sustained alumina-to-aluminum ratio below 1.90 implies feedstock tightness and supports smelter margin compression.

rics.description: Alumina production, Henan Province
rics.meaning: Monthly alumina production in Henan Province, published by the NBS Henan Bureau. Henan is China's largest alumina-producing province (~30% of national output, ~22 Mt/year), home to Chalco Zhongzhou, Henan Shenhuo, and Wanji Aluminium. Henan also hosts significant domestic bauxite reserves, giving it feedstock advantages over coastal alumina refineries dependent on imported ore.
rics.how_to_use: Henan's monthly output is the single most important provincial alumina read — a production cut here (due to environmental inspections, power rationing, or mine safety closures) immediately tightens the national alumina balance. Henan output declines of >5% MoM during winter heating season (Nov–Mar) are common due to air-quality curtailment orders and historically correlate with a 3-8% alumina spot price spike within 4-6 weeks.

rics.description: Aluminum production, Anhui Province
rics.meaning: Monthly primary aluminum (electrolytic aluminum) production in Anhui Province, published by the NBS Anhui Bureau. Anhui is a second-tier aluminum producer with ~1.5 Mt/year capacity, home to Chinalco Ruimin and several smaller smelters. The province benefits from Yangtze River electricity access but lacks abundant cheap hydropower relative to Yunnan or Xinjiang.
rics.how_to_use: Anhui aluminum output is useful as a 'base-load' coal-power smelter indicator — unlike Yunnan (hydro-dependent) or Xinjiang (coal surplus), Anhui margins are tightly linked to national coal and electricity prices. When Anhui output is rising while Yunnan is cutting (aCNCNDRRM1), it signals relative grid-power cost competitiveness has shifted. Compare with aCNCNKRWSM to verify alumina supply adequacy.

rics.description: Aluminum production, Beijing Municipality
rics.meaning: Monthly primary aluminum production in Beijing Municipality, published by the NBS Beijing Bureau. Beijing's aluminum smelting capacity is minimal and in long-term structural decline due to environmental regulations (Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei blue-sky policies). Output is primarily from recycling and downstream aluminum fabrication rather than primary electrolytic smelting.
rics.how_to_use: This series is of limited value as a standalone production indicator given Beijing's negligible primary smelting scale (<50 kt/year). More useful as a proxy for secondary/recycled aluminum activity in the capital's manufacturing base. A persistent decline confirms Beijing's industrial restructuring away from energy-intensive primary metals — relevant context for national capacity relocation trends toward Xinjiang and Yunnan.

rics.description: Aluminum production, Fujian Province[e]
rics.meaning: Monthly primary aluminum production in Fujian Province, published by the NBS Fujian Bureau (marked [e] indicating estimated/unofficial data). Fujian is a minor aluminum producer but a significant aluminum fabrication hub — particularly for aluminum profiles used in construction and electronics exported through Xiamen and Fuzhou ports.
rics.how_to_use: The [e] flag means treat as a directional indicator rather than a precise volume benchmark; revisions can be material. Fujian output growth primarily reflects downstream fabrication activity (extrusions, profiles) rather than primary smelting expansion. When Fujian output is rising alongside robust export data (aCNCEXBA), it typically signals strong overseas demand for Chinese aluminum semi-finished products.

rics.description: Aluminum production, Guangdong Province
rics.meaning: Monthly primary and secondary aluminum production in Guangdong Province, published by the NBS Guangdong Bureau. Guangdong is China's largest aluminum fabrication and recycling province (~3 Mt/year processed), though primary smelting is limited by high electricity costs. The province hosts major secondary aluminum smelters and extrusion operations serving the Pearl River Delta's auto, electronics, and construction sectors.
rics.how_to_use: Guangdong's aluminum data predominantly reflects secondary/recycled output and value-added fabrication rather than primary electrolysis. When Guangdong output rises in tandem with export volumes (aCNCEXBA), it signals strong global demand for Chinese aluminium die-castings and extrusions — the primary EV component supply chain. Cross with aCNCNLEGIM (Guangdong crude steel) to assess relative metals sector health in China's wealthiest province.

rics.description: Aluminum production, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, Cumulative
rics.meaning: Monthly cumulative (year-to-date) primary aluminum production in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, published by the NBS Guangxi Bureau. Guangxi has emerged as a significant aluminum hub (~3 Mt/year capacity) leveraging its large domestic bauxite reserves (the largest in southern China) and the Pingguo and Baise bauxite belts that feed Chalco's Guangxi smelters.
rics.how_to_use: Cumulative-basis data is most useful for year-on-year growth comparisons — derive monthly incremental figures by differencing consecutive months. Guangxi growth above 8% YoY on a cumulative basis indicates brownfield capacity addition or ramp-up of idled smelters responding to improved aluminium prices. Guangxi's bauxite integration gives it cost advantages over provinces relying on imported ore from Guinea or Australia.

rics.description: Aluminum production, Heilongjiang Province
rics.meaning: Monthly primary aluminum production in Heilongjiang Province, published by the NBS Heilongjiang Bureau. Heilongjiang is a minor aluminum producer in northeast China, with smelting activity limited by high coal costs and aging industrial infrastructure. Output is primarily from the Jianlong Aluminiu operation and smaller secondary smelters serving local auto parts manufacturing.
rics.how_to_use: Low absolute volumes make this series most useful as a northeast China industrial health indicator. Rising Heilongjiang aluminum output despite high regional power costs implies strong local fabrication demand or policy-driven smelter restarts. Cross with aCNCNIAVM (Heilongjiang crude steel) to assess whether the province's heavy industry base is broadly recovering or in continued structural contraction.

rics.description: Aluminum production, Henan Province
rics.meaning: Monthly primary aluminum production in Henan Province, published by the NBS Henan Bureau — one of two Henan aluminum RICs in this batch (see also aCNCNRXUXM), likely reflecting different data vintages or revised methodology. Henan is China's #1 aluminum-producing province (~9 Mt/year, ~28% of national output), dominated by Wanji, Shenhuo, and Chalco Zhongzhou operations.
rics.how_to_use: Henan aluminum output is the single most important provincial aluminum data point. Environmental curtailment orders (typically Q1 and Q4) can cut Henan output by 10-15% seasonally, which historically drives a 2-5% LME aluminum price response. When this series deviates from aCNCNRXUXM by >5%, verify which represents current-period versus cumulative methodology before drawing conclusions.

rics.description: Aluminum production, Henan Province
rics.meaning: Monthly primary aluminum production in Henan Province — second data series from the NBS Henan Bureau, potentially representing a revised or alternative statistical compilation from aCNCNTPTOM. Both series measure the same underlying provincial output but may use different enterprise samples, base-year deflators, or cumulative vs. current-period measurement conventions.
rics.how_to_use: Run both Henan series (aCNCNTPTOM and this one) together to identify data revisions and assess reporting consistency. The spread between the two is a useful quality-control check: convergence indicates alignment between provincial and national NBS data systems; persistent divergence suggests methodology differences requiring reconciliation before use in supply models. Use the lower of the two as the conservative base case for Henan supply modelling.

rics.description: Aluminum production, Hubei Province
rics.meaning: Monthly primary aluminum production in Hubei Province, published by the NBS Hubei Bureau. Hubei hosts around 1.2 Mt/year of aluminum capacity, anchored by Jinjiang Aluminium and China Zhongwang's Hubei operations. The Three Gorges hydropower corridor gives Hubei access to renewable electricity, though less exclusively than Yunnan.
rics.how_to_use: Hubei aluminum production is a useful mid-China indicator bridging the coal-power dominated north and hydro-dominated south. When Hubei output diverges from Yunnan (aCNCNDRRM1), it typically reflects Hubei's grid-power vs. Yunnan's hydro seasonality differential — Yunnan cuts in dry-season Q1 while Hubei holds steadier. Compare with local electricity price schedules to estimate smelter margin.

rics.description: Aluminum production, Jiangxi Province
rics.meaning: Monthly primary aluminum production in Jiangxi Province, published by the NBS Jiangxi Bureau. Jiangxi is better known for non-ferrous metals — copper (Jiangxi Copper is headquartered in Guixi), rare earths, and tungsten — than for aluminum; aluminum output is modest (~0.5 Mt/year) and secondary-focused, serving the province's extensive auto and electronics downstream.
rics.how_to_use: Jiangxi aluminum data is most informative when cross-referenced with its copper output (aCNCNDQMEM) to assess the province's broader non-ferrous industrial health. A coordinated rise in both aluminum and copper production suggests the province is running hot on refining capacity — watch for power supply bottlenecks. Jiangxi is also a key rare earth processing province; aluminum and rare earth activity often move together with State Grid investment cycles.

rics.description: Aluminum production, Jilin Province, Current Period
rics.meaning: Monthly current-period primary aluminum production in Jilin Province, published by the NBS Jilin Bureau. Jilin is a minor aluminum producer in northeast China with <0.5 Mt/year capacity, primarily in secondary/recycled aluminum serving local auto parts manufacturing (FAW Group's home base). The 'Current Period' label confirms this is a point-in-time monthly flow rather than a cumulative YTD figure.
rics.how_to_use: Low volumes limit standalone significance, but Jilin aluminum is useful as a northeast China industrial activity proxy. When Jilin and Heilongjiang (aCNCNCVMHM) aluminum output rise simultaneously, it suggests auto sector restocking is driving secondary aluminum demand in the northeast's legacy manufacturing belt. Cross with aCNCNIIPUM (Jilin crude steel) for a composite northeast metals picture.

rics.description: Aluminum production, Qinghai Province
rics.meaning: Monthly primary aluminum production in Qinghai Province, published by the NBS Qinghai Bureau. Qinghai is a fast-growing aluminum province (~3 Mt/year capacity, ~9% of national output) powered entirely by hydroelectricity from Yellow River dams. The province has attracted significant investment from Qinghai Salt Lake Industry and SPIC (State Power Investment Corp) precisely because of its green-power credentials for low-carbon aluminum.
rics.how_to_use: Qinghai is the purest hydropower-aluminum play in China's national grid: output tracks Yellow River water levels and reservoir storage, peaking in wet season (May–October). When Qinghai output surges >15% YoY, it typically reflects new hydro-smelter capacity commission rather than existing-plant ramp-up — a leading indicator of future LME aluminum supply increases. Green aluminum premiums (~$50-100/t over standard LME) make Qinghai output increasingly attractive to ESG-focused European buyers.

rics.description: Aluminum production, Shanxi Province
rics.meaning: Monthly primary aluminum production in Shanxi Province, published by the NBS Shanxi Bureau. Shanxi (~2 Mt/year aluminum capacity) leverages its vast coal resources for captive power generation at integrated coal-alumina-aluminum operations — notably Shanxi Huaze Aluminium and several Chalco subsidiaries. Shanxi also has significant alumina refining capacity (aCNCNKRWSM national aggregate includes Shanxi).
rics.how_to_use: Shanxi aluminum output is a coal-power-aluminium integration barometer: when Shanxi coal prices are low relative to national grid tariffs, Shanxi captive-power smelters gain competitive advantage over grid-powered peers. A Shanxi output rise accompanied by Shanxi coal price declines (track via Taiyuan spot) is a margin expansion signal for the province's integrated aluminum producers. Compare with Henan (aCNCNTPTOM) for the coal-province aluminum competition dynamic.

rics.description: Aluminum production, Sichuan Province
rics.meaning: Monthly primary aluminum production in Sichuan Province, published by the NBS Sichuan Bureau. Sichuan (~1.8 Mt/year capacity) sits at the intersection of hydro-rich southwest China and the legacy Chengdu-Chongqing industrial belt; producers include Sichuan Guangan and Sichuan Qiyuan, powered by Min River and Dadu River hydropower. Output is highly seasonal — elevated in wet season, curtailed in dry-season power shortages.
rics.how_to_use: Sichuan aluminum is heavily affected by dry-season power rationing (typically Jan–May): the August 2022 Sichuan power crisis cut provincial aluminum output ~30% in a single month and caused a temporary LME spike. Track alongside Yunnan (aCNCNDRRM1) as the two key hydro-aluminum provinces; simultaneous dry-season cuts in both can tighten China's domestic aluminum supply by 1.5-2 Mt annualised, a material market signal.

rics.description: Aluminum production, Tianjin Municipality
rics.meaning: Monthly primary and secondary aluminum production in Tianjin Municipality, published by the NBS Tianjin Bureau. Tianjin's aluminum activity is primarily secondary/recycled (auto parts scrap, industrial scrap remelting) and downstream fabrication (foil, sheet) rather than primary electrolytic smelting. The port city's role as China's northern metals trading hub gives it access to scrap imports and LME-linked pricing.
rics.how_to_use: Tianjin aluminum data is a useful secondary/recycled metals proxy — when import scrap flows increase (track Customs data on HS 7602), Tianjin output typically rises with a 4-6 week lag. Compare with aCNCNPCBM (Tianjin crude steel) to assess the municipality's overall metals intensity. Rising aluminum alongside falling steel in Tianjin signals a structural shift toward lighter-material manufacturing in the Bohai Rim industrial zone.

rics.description: Aluminum production, Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region,Current Period
rics.meaning: Monthly current-period primary aluminum production in Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region, published by the NBS Xinjiang Bureau. Xinjiang has become China's fastest-growing aluminum province (~7 Mt/year, ~22% of national output) due to abundant and cheap coal-fired power (~0.25 CNY/kWh for industrial users, the lowest in China), attracting massive capacity relocation from coastal provinces since 2017.
rics.how_to_use: Xinjiang is the dominant marginal supply driver in China's aluminum market — when new capacity comes online here, it directly depresses the national cost curve. Monthly output above 600 kt signals continued capacity expansion; at the current ~7 Mt/year run-rate, Xinjiang alone exceeds the entire EU's aluminum production. This series carries geopolitical risk premium: US/EU Uyghur forced-labour legislation (UFLPA) has created a growing two-tier market with Xinjiang aluminum commanding discounts in Western-linked supply chains.

rics.description: Aluminum production, Yunnan Province, Current Period
rics.meaning: Monthly current-period primary aluminum production in Yunnan Province, published by the NBS Yunnan Bureau. Yunnan (~5 Mt/year peak capacity, ~15% of national output) is China's dominant hydropower-aluminum province, with smelters run by Yunnan Aluminium, Yunnan Shenhuo, and Chalco relying almost entirely on Lancang River hydropower. Output swings dramatically between wet (May–October) and dry (November–April) seasons.
rics.how_to_use: Yunnan is THE most market-moving provincial aluminum series: a government-mandated curtailment order (as in 2023, cutting ~1 Mt/year of capacity) triggers LME cash/3-month backwardation and a typical $50-150/t price spike within 2 weeks. The dry season cut (Nov–Apr) is structural and priced in, but unusual wet-season curtailments are market surprises. When Yunnan output drops >10% MoM in wet season, it signals extraordinary power supply failure and warrants immediate portfolio review of aluminum longs.

rics.description: Aluminum production, Zhejiang Province
rics.meaning: Monthly primary and secondary aluminum production in Zhejiang Province, published by the NBS Zhejiang Bureau. Zhejiang is a major aluminum processing and fabrication centre (~1.5 Mt/year) but minimal in primary smelting. Zhejiang hosts Yongjin Metal Technology, Zhongfu Industrial, and numerous aluminum profile and foil producers serving packaging, construction, and consumer electronics export markets.
rics.how_to_use: Zhejiang's aluminum output is best interpreted as a value-added fabrication indicator: when it rises, downstream export demand for packaging foil, automotive trim, and electronics components is strong. Compare with Guangdong (aCNCNLRUDM) — together they represent China's two biggest downstream aluminum fabrication hubs. Rising Zhejiang output alongside strong export data (aCNCEXBA) points to healthy global demand for Chinese aluminum semis.

rics.meaning: Cumulative year-on-year growth rate of business costs (operating costs) at industrial companies above designated size in the coal mining and washing industry, published monthly by the NBS. Covers wages, materials, energy, and depreciation across the NBS's survey universe of coal firms with annual revenue >CNY 20M — capturing roughly 80% of national coal output.
rics.how_to_use: When this cost growth rate exceeds revenue growth (track against sales value data), it signals margin compression for the coal sector — a precursor to production cuts at high-cost mines and potential credit stress in coal-related bond markets (particularly Shanxi and Inner Mongolia SOEs). Cost growth above 10% YoY for three consecutive months has historically preceded NBS warnings about coal sector financial health and policy support measures.

rics.description: Business cost, industrial companies above designated size, electricity, heat production & supply ,Cumulative
rics.subcategory: Electricity, Heat Production & Supply — Business Cost (Cumulative)
rics.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date business/operating cost for industrial companies above designated size in the electricity, heat production and supply sector. Published monthly by NBS as part of the Industrial Enterprise Financial Statistics dataset, typically released ~27th of the following month. Captures fuel procurement, depreciation, and maintenance costs for China's power generation and district heating complex.
rics.how_to_use: Monitor as a cost-push pressure gauge for the power sector — rapid acceleration vs. the prior year cumulative often reflects coal price shocks passing through to utility cost structures. When cumulative costs grow faster than cumulative revenue (cross-reference aCNCNFBSKM), utility sector profitability compresses and can signal upcoming tariff reform discussions. Useful for evaluating state-owned power generators (Huaneng, Datang) credit risk.

rics.description: Business cost, industrial companies above designated size, electricity, heat production & supply ,Year on Year ,Cumulative
rics.subcategory: Electricity, Heat Production & Supply — Business Cost YoY (Cumulative)
rics.meaning: Year-on-year cumulative business cost for industrial companies above designated size in the electricity, heat production and supply sector, expressed as the current-period cumulative absolute value compared to the same period of the prior year. Published monthly by NBS, typically ~27th of the following month. Paired with aCNCNYKGUM which gives the raw cumulative level.
rics.how_to_use: The YoY comparison format makes it easier to assess real cost acceleration without seasonal distortions. A cumulative cost surge of 15-20%+ YoY historically accompanies coal price spikes (2021 was a notable episode with thermal coal hitting CNY 2,500/tonne). Practitioners use this alongside power sector revenue growth to infer tariff adequacy and potential grid subsidy flows.

rics.description: Business cost, industrial companies above designated size, electricity, heat production & supply ,Year on Year Growth ,Cumulative
rics.subcategory: Electricity, Heat Production & Supply — Business Cost YoY Growth (Cumulative)
rics.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of cumulative business costs for industrial companies above designated size in the electricity, heat production and supply sector. Published monthly by NBS, typically around the 27th of the following month. This is the percentage change format of the cost series, enabling direct cross-sector comparisons of cost inflation dynamics.
rics.how_to_use: A reading above 10% YoY cumulative growth flags significant cost-push pressure in utilities — the 2021 energy crisis saw this series spike to 30%+ as coal shortages emerged. Persistent above-average cost growth without corresponding tariff increases compresses ROE at state-owned power firms and is a leading indicator of NDRC market-based electricity pricing policy adjustments. Compare with the PPI for electricity (aCNCNFBSKM) to assess pass-through.

rics.description: Business cost, industrial companies above designated size, electricity, heat, gas & water production & supply ,Year on Year Growth ,Cumulative
rics.subcategory: Electricity, Heat, Gas & Water — Business Cost YoY Growth (Cumulative)
rics.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of cumulative business costs for industrial companies above designated size across the combined electricity, heat, gas and water production and supply sector. Published monthly by NBS, typically ~27th of the following month. This broader aggregate adds gas distribution and water supply firms to the electricity/heat cost base tracked by aCNCNCBIM1.
rics.how_to_use: The electricity+heat+gas+water composite cost gauge is most relevant during commodity price cycles — natural gas procurement costs (dominated by CNOOC, PipeChina imports) add a distinct LNG/pipeline gas price dimension absent from the power-only series. When gas costs surge (2021-22 LNG spike), this composite reads 5-8 ppts higher than the electricity-only series. Used by analysts covering CGN, ENN Energy, and Beijing Gas equity valuations.

rics.description: Business cost, industrial companies above designated size, printing & recording media reproduction ,Year on Year Growth ,Cumulative
rics.subcategory: Printing Industry Business Cost — YoY Cumulative
rics.meaning: Cumulative year-on-year growth rate of business costs at industrial companies above designated size in the printing and recording media reproduction industry, published monthly by the NBS. While technically outside the metals/mining core, this series is included in the batch as part of a broader NBS industrial cost dataset covering multiple manufacturing sub-sectors.
rics.how_to_use: Use primarily as a cross-sector benchmark for industrial cost inflation trends — comparing printing-sector cost growth against metals/mining cost growth (aCNCNDPCM) helps isolate commodity-specific cost drivers (energy, raw materials) from economy-wide labor/logistics inflation. Elevated printing costs relative to metals can signal wage inflation is broadening beyond resource-intensive sectors.

rics.description: Business cost, industrial companies above designated size, railway, marine, aerospace & other transportation equipment ,Cumulative
rics.subcategory: Railway, Marine, Aerospace & Other Transport Equipment — Business Cost (Cumulative)
rics.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date business/operating cost for industrial companies above designated size in the railway, marine, aerospace and other transportation equipment manufacturing sector. Published monthly by NBS, typically around the 27th of the following month. This sub-sector includes CRRC rail rolling stock, Jiangnan shipbuilding, and AVIC aerospace components.
rics.how_to_use: Rising cumulative costs alongside robust new order announcements (e.g., CRRC metro train tenders) generally reflect healthy demand-driven scale-up rather than margin squeeze. Key cost components are steel (rail cars), aluminum (aerospace), and specialized electronics. A cost growth rate exceeding 12-15% YoY without commensurate revenue gains signals margin deterioration — relevant for pricing BRI infrastructure-linked transport OEM export competitiveness.

rics.description: Business cost, industrial companies above designated size, special equipment manufacturing ,Cumulative
rics.meaning: Cumulative year-to-date business/operating cost for industrial companies above designated size in the special equipment manufacturing sub-sector. Published monthly by NBS around the 27th of the following month. Special equipment in China's industrial classification includes mining machinery, metallurgical equipment, construction machinery (XCMG, Sany, Zoomlion), agricultural machinery, and environmental protection equipment.
rics.how_to_use: Cumulative cost expansion above 8% YoY typically coincides with an infrastructure investment upcycle — watch alongside FAI in manufacturing (NDRC monthly) and excavator sales (CCMA data, typically 15,000-25,000 units/month in upcycle). Sany and XCMG sales volumes correlate closely. Deceleration of cost growth below 3% flags excess capacity — construction machinery saw this dynamic in 2014-15 and again in late 2022-23.

rics.description: Business income, industrial companies above designated size, coal mining & washing industry, Qinghai Province
rics.meaning: Business income (revenue) of industrial companies above designated size in the coal mining and washing industry in Qinghai Province, published irregularly by the NBS Qinghai Bureau. Qinghai has modest coal output relative to Shanxi or Inner Mongolia, but its coal sector is strategically important for the plateau province's power supply and heating given limited grid interconnection with the national network.
rics.how_to_use: Irregular frequency limits time-series utility; use as a snapshot of the revenue trajectory for Qinghai's coal SOEs. Cross with aCNCNDJUWM (Qinghai aluminum) — when coal revenues fall (implying lower production/prices) while aluminum output rises, it signals the province is accelerating its energy transition from coal power to hydro-powered aluminum, consistent with policy direction.

rics.description: Cast iron production
rics.meaning: Monthly cast iron production in China (Series A), published by the NBS. Cast iron (pig iron cast into foundry shapes or continued into blast furnace production) is a key upstream steel input — China produces ~700-800 Mt/year of pig iron, of which the bulk is used in steelmaking BOFs; the remainder goes to foundry cast iron for machinery, pipes, and automotive components.
rics.how_to_use: Compare this series with aCNCNFMQOM (second cast iron series) and aCNPDPIGI (pig iron production) to reconcile across data sources. Rising cast iron output alongside flat crude steel (aCNCNBFWHM) may indicate foundry/casting sector demand is outpacing steelmaking demand — a positive signal for industrial machinery and infrastructure casting orders. Monthly output below 55 Mt signals iron balance tightness.

rics.description: Cast iron production
rics.meaning: Monthly cast iron production in China (Series B) — a second NBS data series that may reflect a different enterprise sample, revised methodology, or alternative classification within the NBS industrial production system. Both Series A (aCNCNQCCRM) and this series measure foundry and pig iron casting output at above-designated-size industrial enterprises.
rics.how_to_use: Run both cast iron series together as a quality-control pair: persistent divergence of >3% suggests methodology differences worth investigating before building iron ore demand models. When both series trend down simultaneously with pig iron (aCNPDPIGI) also declining, it confirms a genuine slowdown in upstream steelmaking activity — a bearish signal for iron ore futures (DCE i-contracts). Convergence across all three provides high-confidence iron supply read.

rics.description: Cast steel production
rics.meaning: Monthly cast steel (steel castings) production in China, published by the NBS. Cast steel differs from wrought/rolled steel — it is poured into molds to produce heavy industrial components: rolling mill housings, mining equipment frames, locomotive chassis, hydro turbine runners, and large valve bodies. China is the world's largest cast steel producer (~25 Mt/year of castings).
rics.how_to_use: Cast steel production is a capital goods investment cycle indicator — demand is driven by new capacity installation in mining, power generation, rail, and heavy machinery rather than property construction. When cast steel output grows faster than rolled steel (aCNPDSTPR), it signals capital expenditure is accelerating in heavy industries. A persistent cast steel contraction alongside rebar growth is typical of property-led (vs. industrial-led) recovery patterns.

rics.description: Casting machinery production
rics.meaning: Monthly production of casting machinery (foundry equipment — sand casting machines, die-casting machines, centrifugal casting machines) in China, published by the NBS. China is the world's largest casting machinery producer and consumer; equipment output reflects investment intentions in the foundry sector serving auto, machinery, and infrastructure casting demand.
rics.how_to_use: Casting machinery output is a capital investment leading indicator for the foundry industry — orders placed for casting equipment typically precede production ramp-up by 6-12 months. When casting machinery production surges >15% YoY, it points to foundry capacity expansion, particularly in auto aluminium die-casting (driven by EV powertrain lightweighting). Cross with aCNCNMRCUM (powder metallurgy parts) to assess advanced manufacturing metals-processing investment.

rics.description: Coke production
rics.meaning: Monthly metallurgical coke production in China (Series A), published by the NBS. Coke is the essential reducing agent and structural support in blast furnace ironmaking; China produces ~500-550 Mt/year of coke, the world's largest at ~67% of global output. Major coking coal bases are in Shanxi, Shaanxi, and Inner Mongolia; major coke production centres include Shanxi, Hebei, and Shandong.
rics.how_to_use: Coke production moves in lockstep with pig iron and crude steel output — model it at a ~0.42 tonne coke/tonne pig iron ratio. When coke output grows faster than steel (aCNCNBFWHM), it implies coke inventory build at steel mills (bearish for coking coal futures DCE j2509). A coke-to-steel ratio above 0.45 signals BF efficiency deterioration or overcooking — watch for NBS energy efficiency warning releases.

rics.description: Coke production
rics.meaning: Monthly coke production in China (Series B) — second NBS data series, potentially reflecting a different enterprise survey population or revised data vintage from aCNCNBUTGM. Both series cover metallurgical coke (hard coke for blast furnaces) and may also include some oven coke for chemical/fuel uses depending on NBS classification.
rics.how_to_use: Use alongside Series A (aCNCNBUTGM) for triangulation and revision detection. When both coke series fall >5% YoY simultaneously, it reliably confirms blast furnace utilisation rates are declining — a strong bearish signal for coking coal and iron ore simultaneously. The two-series approach also helps detect seasonal distortions (Chinese New Year, winter heating season) that affect survey response rates differently across enterprise cohorts.

rics.description: Copper production
rics.meaning: Monthly refined copper (electrolytic copper, cathode copper) production in China, published by the NBS. China is the world's largest refined copper producer (~45% of global output, ~12 Mt/year), processing both domestic concentrate and ~70% imported concentrate. Key producers include Jiangxi Copper, Tongling Nonferrous, Yunnan Copper, and Jinchuan Group.
rics.how_to_use: China refined copper output is a critical input for global copper supply models — every 1% change in Chinese output equals ~120 kt of annual supply. Compare monthly against LME copper inventory changes and China bonded warehouse stocks: rising output combined with rising inventories is structurally bearish; rising output with falling stocks signals robust downstream demand (power cables, EVs, electronics). Typical monthly output 900-1,000 kt; a print above 1,050 kt is a market-moving supply surprise.

rics.description: Copper production, Guangdong Province
rics.meaning: Monthly refined copper production in Guangdong Province, published by the NBS Guangdong Bureau. Guangdong is a major copper refining province (~1.5 Mt/year, ~13% of national output), anchored by Guangdong Shaoguan Smelter (a Jiangxi Copper subsidiary) and multiple downstream copper tube/rod fabricators in the Pearl River Delta serving air-conditioning, automotive, and electronics end-markets.
rics.how_to_use: Guangdong copper output is closely tied to electronics and EV supply chain demand — a meaningful share of Guangdong's copper output feeds directly into printed circuit boards, power connectors, and EV wiring harnesses produced for export. When Guangdong copper rises alongside strong export electronics data (aCNCEXBA), it confirms healthy global tech demand. Track against aCNCNDQMEM (national) to compute Guangdong's share — above 14% implies the province is running above capacity utilisation.

rics.description: Copper production, Tianjin Municipality
rics.meaning: Monthly refined copper production in Tianjin Municipality, published by the NBS Tianjin Bureau. Tianjin hosts secondary copper smelting and copper alloy fabrication rather than large-scale primary refining; capacity focuses on copper rod, tube, and foil for the Bohai Rim's auto, HVAC, and power equipment manufacturing clusters.
rics.how_to_use: Tianjin copper output is a useful indicator for northern China copper fabrication demand — when it rises, it signals healthy automotive and power equipment production in the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region. Cross with aCNCNPCBM (Tianjin steel) and aCNCNGHSEM (Tianjin aluminum) for a comprehensive Bohai Rim heavy industry dashboard. A Tianjin copper output decline often precedes downstream auto OEM production cuts by 4-6 weeks.

rics.description: Cost in main business income of industrial enterprises above designated size, electricity, heat, gas & water production & supply
rics.subcategory: Electricity, Heat, Gas & Water — Cost-to-Revenue Ratio
rics.units: %, cost as share of main business income
rics.meaning: Business cost as a percentage of main business income for industrial companies above designated size in the electricity, heat, gas and water production and supply sector. Published monthly by NBS as part of the Industrial Enterprise Financial Statistics. This ratio directly measures operating efficiency/profitability of the utility sector, complementing the absolute cost level (aCNCNYKGUM).
rics.how_to_use: A cost-to-revenue ratio above 85% for the utilities composite signals near-zero operating margins — China's grid operators historically hover around 78-82% in stable coal-price environments, but spiked above 90% in 2021 when coal costs surged while regulated tariffs lagged. Practitioners use this series to anticipate NDRC tariff adjustments and model state grid (SGCC/CSG) capex capacity. Sharp ratio deterioration often precedes subsidy policy announcements.

rics.description: Crude steel production
rics.meaning: Monthly national crude steel production (all methods: BOF, EAF, open-hearth) published by the NBS — China's headline steel output series and one of the most watched industrial statistics globally. China produces ~1,000-1,050 Mt/year (~50% of global supply); released around the 15th of the following month. The NBS series covers all industrial enterprises above designated size.
rics.how_to_use: THE key China steel indicator. Market threshold: monthly output above 90 Mt (1,080 Mt annualised) triggers government output-cap concern; below 82 Mt signals aggressive curtailment. YoY growth above 5% typically drives iron ore futures (DCE i2509) up $5-10/t within days. Cross-check with CISA key-enterprise data (aCNCNCOSM) released ~2 weeks earlier to gauge revision risk. Post-2020, production 'capping' directives have increased the policy uncertainty around this series.

rics.description: Crude steel production, Beijing Municipality
rics.meaning: Monthly crude steel production in Beijing Municipality, published by the NBS Beijing Bureau. Beijing's steelmaking capacity has been substantially eliminated under clean-air policy — Shougang Group relocated its Beijing mills to Caofeidian (Hebei coast) by 2010. Residual output is primarily from scrap-based EAF operations serving specialty steel for the capital's manufacturing and construction sectors.
rics.how_to_use: Beijing crude steel output is negligible in absolute terms (<2 Mt/year) and declining — primarily useful as a policy implementation tracker. Sustained near-zero output confirms Beijing's industrial restructuring success. Cross with aCNCNJWBM (Beijing aluminum) and aCNCNLQBDM (Hebei steel — where Shougang capacity was relocated) to trace the spatial shift in China's steel industry geography.

rics.description: Crude steel production, Chongqing Municipality
rics.meaning: Monthly crude steel production in Chongqing Municipality, published by the NBS Chongqing Bureau. Chongqing (~10 Mt/year crude steel capacity) is the key southwestern steel producer, home to Chongqing Iron and Steel (Chonggang) and Jianlong Chongqing. The municipality's steel sector serves auto manufacturing (Changan Automobile, Lifan), rail equipment (CRRC), and Yangtze River infrastructure.
rics.how_to_use: Chongqing steel output is a southwest China industrial activity indicator particularly sensitive to auto production cycles — Chongqing is China's largest single-city auto manufacturing hub. When Chongqing steel and Guangdong steel (aCNCNLEGIM) both rise, it signals broad national manufacturing recovery rather than a property-specific rebound. Monthly output above 900 kt indicates the municipality's mills are running at near-full capacity.

rics.description: Crude steel production, Guangdong Province
rics.meaning: Monthly crude steel production in Guangdong Province, published by the NBS Guangdong Bureau. Guangdong (~40 Mt/year crude steel capacity) is a major southern steel producer, anchored by Baowu's Zhanjiang stainless/specialty complex, HBIS Guangzhou, and Shaoguan Iron and Steel. Guangdong steel primarily serves the province's auto, electronics, and export-oriented machinery industries.
rics.how_to_use: Guangdong steel is a proxy for export-oriented manufacturing steel demand (appliances, auto, shipping containers) rather than property construction. When Guangdong output rises strongly but northern provinces (Hebei aCNCNLQBDM, Shanxi aCNCNGKNRM) stagnate, it signals demand is shifting from infrastructure/property to industrial/export end-uses — a structural rather than cyclical recovery pattern. Compare against aCNCNTPZM (Guangdong copper) for a composite southern China metals picture.

rics.description: Crude steel production, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, Current Period
rics.meaning: Monthly current-period crude steel production in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, published by the NBS Guangxi Bureau. Guangxi (~20 Mt/year crude steel capacity) has grown rapidly via Baowu's Fangchenggang coastal mill (integrated with ASEAN iron ore imports) and Guangxi Shenglong. The 'Current Period' label confirms this is a flow series, not cumulative YTD.
rics.how_to_use: Guangxi steel is strategically important as China's primary steel export gateway to ASEAN — Fangchenggang port exports significant volumes to Vietnam, the Philippines, and Thailand. When Guangxi output rises faster than domestic demand indicators, watch for steel export surge data (aCNCEXBA) within 4-8 weeks. Guangxi's coastal location also means iron ore supply comes primarily from spot imports (Brazilian/Australian cargoes) rather than domestic ore — making it sensitive to Vale/BHP shipping schedules.

rics.description: Crude steel production, Heilongjiang Province
rics.meaning: Monthly crude steel production in Heilongjiang Province, published by the NBS Heilongjiang Bureau. Heilongjiang is a shrinking steel producer in China's northeast rust belt — capacity has declined from peak levels as demand-side weakness (property contraction, manufacturing migration south) has eroded mill economics. Key producers include Heilongjiang Jianlong Steel.
rics.how_to_use: Heilongjiang steel output is useful as a northeast rust belt recovery indicator. Prolonged output decline here reflects structural demand destruction rather than cyclical slowdown — cross with aCNCNCVMHM (Heilongjiang aluminum) and aCNCNDNCXM (Heilongjiang steel alternate series) to confirm broad provincial industrial contraction. When the northeast bottoms (all series simultaneously trough), it can signal policy-driven revitalisation investment cycles, as Beijing has historically intervened to support northeast industrial SOEs.

rics.description: Crude steel production, Henan Province
rics.meaning: Monthly crude steel production in Henan Province, published by the NBS Henan Bureau. Henan (~30 Mt/year crude steel capacity) is a major central China steelmaker, anchored by Jianlong Zhongyuan and Ansteel Henan. Henan steel demand is driven by the province's massive construction sector (population ~100 million) and growing auto/machinery manufacturing base around Zhengzhou.
rics.how_to_use: Henan is one of China's most populous provinces, so steel output here closely tracks domestic residential construction activity — a direct housing demand barometer. When Henan steel output falls alongside Hebei (aCNCNLQBDM), it confirms a nationwide property-driven steel demand contraction; when Henan holds up while coastal provinces cut, central infrastructure stimulus is supporting demand. Monthly output above 2.5 Mt indicates full capacity utilisation.

rics.description: Crude steel production, Jiangxi Province
rics.meaning: Monthly crude steel production in Jiangxi Province, published by the NBS Jiangxi Bureau. Jiangxi's steel sector (~8 Mt/year capacity) is smaller relative to its non-ferrous metals industry; key producers include Xinyu Steel and Fangda Steel. The province's steel output primarily serves local construction, auto (JAC Motors in Hefei, close border), and machinery sectors.
rics.how_to_use: Cross with aCNCNDMDIM (Jiangxi aluminum) and aCNCNDQMEM (national copper) to assess Jiangxi's composite metals cycle — the province is unique in having significant production across steel, copper, rare earths, and tungsten simultaneously, making it a rare cross-commodity industrial barometer. When Jiangxi steel rises concurrently with copper refining, it indicates a broad provincial industrial upturn rather than a sector-specific move.

rics.description: Crude steel production, Jilin Province, Current Period
rics.subcategory: Crude Steel Production — Jilin Province (Current Period)
rics.meaning: Monthly current-period crude steel production in Jilin Province, published by the NBS Jilin Bureau. Jilin (~5 Mt/year crude steel capacity) is the smallest steel producer among northeast provinces; key producers include Tonghua Iron and Steel and Jilin Iron and Steel. The province's auto sector (FAW Group headquarters in Changchun) is the primary steel consumer.
rics.how_to_use: Jilin steel output is primarily a FAW auto supply chain indicator — when Jilin steel production tracks above prior-year levels, FAW's Changchun plants (Audi joint venture, FAW-Toyota) are likely running at elevated production schedules. Cross with aCNCNFZESM (Jilin aluminum) and aCNCNIIPUM to build a composite Jilin auto metals demand picture. Monthly output consistently below 400 kt signals structural northeast steel overcapacity pressure.

rics.description: Crude steel production, Liaoning Province
rics.meaning: Monthly crude steel production in Liaoning Province, published by the NBS Liaoning Bureau. Liaoning (~50 Mt/year crude steel capacity) is northeast China's largest steel producer and among China's top five nationally, anchored by Ansteel (Angang Steel — Baowu's northeast subsidiary), Benxi Steel, and Fushun Special Steel. Liaoning steel feeds the province's shipbuilding, auto, and heavy machinery sectors.
rics.how_to_use: Liaoning steel is the northeast's leading steel indicator — Ansteel alone accounts for ~30 Mt/year. When Liaoning rises while other northeast provinces (aCNCNIAVM, aCNCNIIPUM) contract, it signals Ansteel is gaining market share through scale advantages. Cross with aCNCNOTAM (Liaoning total steel including all grades) to assess the crude/finished steel conversion ratio for the province's integrated mills. Monthly output above 4.2 Mt implies near-full blast furnace utilisation.

rics.description: Crude steel production, Shaanxi Province
rics.meaning: Monthly crude steel production in Shaanxi Province, published by the NBS Shaanxi Bureau. Shaanxi (~15 Mt/year crude steel capacity) is a significant northwest China steelmaker, anchored by Longmen Steel (Shaanxi Iron and Steel Group) in Hancheng and Baoji Special Steel for aerospace/defence applications. Shaanxi's steel sector is uniquely positioned near northwest infrastructure mega-projects (Belt and Road trans-Eurasian corridors).
rics.how_to_use: Shaanxi steel output is a northwest infrastructure and energy-sector demand indicator — steel consumption here is dominated by pipeline construction (energy corridors through Shaanxi to Xinjiang and Central Asia), rail projects, and coal-chemical industry equipment. When Shaanxi output rises during periods of flat or declining national output (aCNCNBFWHM), it typically signals government-directed northwest infrastructure stimulus spending.

rics.description: Crude steel production, Shanxi Province
rics.meaning: Monthly crude steel production in Shanxi Province, published by the NBS Shanxi Bureau. Shanxi (~55 Mt/year crude steel capacity) is China's third-largest steel-producing province after Hebei and Jiangsu, producing primarily long products (rebar, wire rod) alongside coking coal-integrated steelmaking at Taiyuan Iron and Steel (TISCO — world's largest stainless producer), Jianlong Shanxi, and China Baowu Tagang.
rics.how_to_use: Shanxi steel is the coking coal integration play — TISCO and other Shanxi mills operate with captive coking coal mines, giving them cost-curve advantages during periods of high coking coal prices. When Shanxi output is rising while Hebei (aCNCNLQBDM) is cut by environmental orders, it implies Shanxi mills are running harder to capture market share. TISCO stainless output makes this series partially a proxy for stainless/specialty steel demand from appliance and chemical sectors.

rics.description: Crude steel production, Sichuan Province
rics.meaning: Monthly crude steel production in Sichuan Province, published by the NBS Sichuan Bureau. Sichuan (~30 Mt/year crude steel capacity) is southwest China's largest steel producer, anchored by Panzhihua Iron and Steel (Pangang — the world's largest vanadium-titanium steel producer) and Desheng Stainless. Pangang is uniquely positioned with vanadium-titanomagnetite ore reserves in the Panzhihua district.
rics.how_to_use: Sichuan steel has a unique vanadium-titanium angle: Pangang's vanadium pentoxide output (~20% of global supply) makes Sichuan steel output a direct proxy for vanadium market conditions. When Sichuan steel rises strongly, vanadium prices (used in rebar strengthening and vanadium redox flow batteries) typically tighten. The province's rail and infrastructure construction sector (serving the Chengdu–Chongqing mega-region) drives bulk rebar demand.

rics.description: Crude steel production, Tianjin Municipality
rics.meaning: Monthly crude steel production in Tianjin Municipality, published by the NBS Tianjin Bureau. Tianjin (~25 Mt/year crude steel capacity) hosts the Tianjin Iron and Steel Group (TISCO Tianjin) and HBIS Tianjin, with coastal location enabling seaborne iron ore imports directly to Tianjin port. Tianjin produces mainly tubular steel for energy sector, flat products, and specialty steel for Bohai Rim manufacturing.
rics.how_to_use: Tianjin steel output is the oil/gas tubular goods proxy — a significant share of Tianjin flat/tubular production goes to CNPC and Sinopec for energy infrastructure. When Tianjin output rises alongside oil price recovery, it likely reflects energy sector pipeline restocking. Tianjin's port-import iron ore flexibility means its blast furnaces can run at competitive margins even during domestic iron ore price spikes — track against aCNCNMLACM (Beijing) to see the Bohai Rim steel geography.

rics.description: Crude steel production, Yunnan Province, Current Period
rics.subcategory: Crude Steel Production — Yunnan Province (Current Period)
rics.meaning: Monthly current-period crude steel production in Yunnan Province, published by the NBS Yunnan Bureau. Yunnan (~15 Mt/year crude steel capacity) has limited iron ore resources but benefits from scrap availability and access to Mekong River infrastructure markets; Yunnan Metallurgy and Jianlong Yunnan are key producers. The province's output serves ASEAN infrastructure projects and local construction in China's southwest.
rics.how_to_use: Yunnan steel is the ASEAN demand proxy for Chinese long products — when Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia construction activity rises, Yunnan mills are first-mover exporters given geographic proximity. Monitor in conjunction with aCNCNDRRM1 (Yunnan aluminum): when both steel and aluminum are cut simultaneously (as during Yunnan power crises), it signals severe province-wide power rationing — a buying opportunity for both LME aluminum and Asian HRC steel contracts.

rics.description: Crude steel production, Zhejiang Province
rics.meaning: Monthly crude steel production in Zhejiang Province, published by the NBS Zhejiang Bureau. Zhejiang's steel sector (~15 Mt/year capacity) is anchored by Qingshan Industrial's stainless and high-alloy steel complex in Wenzhou — one of the world's largest stainless steel clusters — and Jiulong Steel. The province's steel output is disproportionately concentrated in stainless and special alloy grades rather than commodity rebar.
rics.how_to_use: Zhejiang steel is the stainless steel and high-value alloy indicator in China's provincial data — Qingshan (in Wenzhou/Zhejiang) is the world's #1 NPI (nickel pig iron) consumer and stainless producer. When Zhejiang steel output rises sharply, track nickel prices (LME nickel) — Qingshan's production decisions are the dominant short-term NPI demand signal. A Zhejiang stainless surge concurrent with aCNCNREZD (nickel production) growth confirms a coordinated NPI-stainless expansion cycle.

The quarterly frequency makes it best used as a medium-term strategic overlay rather than a trading trigger — combine with aCNCNKWDNQ (coal mining utilisation) for a broader mining-sector confidence composite.

rics.meaning: Export value of industrial companies above designated size engaged in book and newspaper printing, for foreign, Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwanese-funded enterprises, published irregularly by the NBS. This series is tangential to the metals/mining batch but present as part of the broader NBS industrial statistics universe included in this data collection.
rics.how_to_use: Limited direct relevance to metals/mining; treat as a cross-check on broader industrial export health in the FDI-funded manufacturing segment. When export values from FDI printing firms fall, it can signal broader foreign-funded industrial activity is decelerating — a leading indicator for reduced packaging material (steel tinplate, aluminum foil) demand from the printing/publishing supply chain. Use in conjunction with aCNCNAZHXM (tinplate sales) if packaging demand context is needed.

rics.description: Financial costs, industrial companies above designated size, electricity production
rics.meaning: Financial costs (primarily interest expense) for industrial companies above designated size in the electricity production sector. Published by NBS as part of the Industrial Enterprise Financial Statistics survey; frequency is irregular/annual given the blank frequency field. Captures debt-servicing burden of China's large-scale power generation fleet, dominated by state-owned giants (Huaneng, Datang, Guodian/CHN Energy, Huadian, CPDRC).
rics.how_to_use: Elevated financial costs relative to EBIT (cross-reference with revenue and profit margin data) signal overleveraged power developers — particularly relevant for wind/solar build-out periods when capital expenditure surges. China's five major power groups each carry CNY 400-700 billion in total liabilities; a financial cost-to-revenue ratio above 3-4% historically flags refinancing risk in rate-rising environments. Useful for credit analysts covering power sector bonds.

rics.subcategory: Home Beauty & Health Care Electrical Appliances — Financial Costs
rics.meaning: Financial costs (interest expense and related charges) for industrial companies above designated size in the home beauty and healthcare electrical appliance manufacturing sub-sector. Published by NBS as part of the Industrial Enterprise Financial Statistics; frequency is irregular given the blank field. Covers makers of hair dryers, electric shavers, massage devices, and personal care electronics — a sector dominated by Guangdong-based exporters.
rics.how_to_use: This niche series is most useful as a barometer for small- and medium-sized Guangdong export manufacturers' credit conditions. Financial cost spikes (e.g., tight credit in 2018, COVID in 2020) often presage export order cancellations and inventory destocking. Cross-reference with electronics export data (aCNCEXBA) and USD/CNY to assess FX hedging costs embedded in financials. Sector typically carries low debt given asset-light assembly model.

rics.description: Generator set (power generation equipment) output, Tianjin Municipality
rics.meaning: Monthly output of generator sets (power generation equipment) by industrial enterprises above designated size in Tianjin Municipality. Published by NBS Tianjin Bureau as part of the regional industrial production statistics, typically released in the second or third week of the following month. Tianjin hosts several medium-sized generator set manufacturers supplying both domestic and export markets, including standby diesel generators.
rics.how_to_use: Tianjin generator output is a proxy for backup power equipment demand — peaks typically coincide with rural electrification drives, infrastructure projects, and export surges to Southeast Asia and Africa. Compare with the national generator output series to assess Tianjin's market share. A Tianjin output surge of 20%+ YoY often reflects BRI project equipment procurement cycles. Cross-reference with Xinjiang output (aCNCNTLIOM) for geographic demand pattern contrast.

rics.description: Generator set (power generation equipment) output, Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region, Current Period, Year on Year Growth
rics.subcategory: Generator Set Output — Xinjiang, YoY Growth (Current Period)
rics.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of generator set output in the current period for industrial enterprises above designated size in Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region. Published by NBS Xinjiang Bureau monthly, typically in the second or third week of the following month. Xinjiang has become a significant industrial hub with coal-based power generation infrastructure and equipment manufacturing capacity expansion driven by westward development policies.
rics.how_to_use: Xinjiang generator output growth above 15% YoY signals accelerating industrial build-out in China's western energy base — the region is critical for coal-fired power and increasingly wind/solar hybrid systems. Sharp growth spikes may reflect policy-driven energy security investments post-2021 power crisis. Compare with Tianjin (aCNCNNGGM1) to isolate regional policy vs. market-driven demand effects. Large divergences between Xinjiang and coastal regions highlight east-west industrial policy asymmetry.

rics.description: Harvesting machinery production
rics.meaning: Monthly production of harvesting machinery (combine harvesters, grain threshers, rice harvesters) in China, published by the NBS. China is the world's largest agricultural machinery producer; major producers include XCMG, CNHTC, Zoomlion, and Weichai Power. Harvesting machinery is steel and cast iron-intensive, consuming structural steel, castings, and precision forgings.
rics.how_to_use: Use as an indirect metals demand indicator for the agricultural machinery sector — rising harvesting machinery output implies higher consumption of special steels, castings (aCNCNHAFYM), and precision gears. Cross with aCNCNPGIUM (cast steel) and aCNCNCNPCIHM: a concurrent rise in both harvesting machinery and cast steel production points to broad agricultural equipment cycle expansion, which historically peaks in Q1-Q2 ahead of summer grain harvest seasons.

rics.how_to_use: Henan washing machine output is a useful indicator of inland consumer electronics manufacturing momentum — strong readings (10%+ YoY growth) reflect both domestic demand recovery and import substitution success. Cross-reference with national household appliance retail sales (NBS retail data) to distinguish production-for-inventory from production-for-sale. Correlates with rural consumer credit expansion under China's 'sinking market' (下沉市场) consumption policy.

Anhui is a mid-tier industrial province with boiler manufacturing concentrated around Hefei and Wuhu.
rics.how_to_use: Industrial boiler output in Anhui correlates with provincial heavy industry activity — cement, chemicals, and textile sectors are the primary end-users. A production decline of 10%+ YoY often reflects environmental compliance-driven boiler replacement campaigns (coal-to-gas switching under Blue Sky Action) rather than demand weakness per se. Compare Anhui output against Hebei (aCNCNJWECM/aCNCNLTYHM) to gauge regional environmental compliance timing differences.

Published by NBS Anhui Bureau, typically released in the second or third week of the following month.
rics.how_to_use: Use in conjunction with aCNCNGXRZM to form a complete picture of Anhui's boiler manufacturing sector. Boiler production peaks typically occur in Q3-Q4 ahead of winter heating season procurement. Watch for policy-driven demand surges tied to coal-to-biomass boiler conversions under rural heating restructuring (农村煤改气/煤改电).

rics.description: Industrial boiler production, Beijing Municipality
rics.subcategory: Industrial Boiler Production — Beijing Municipality (Series A)
rics.units: tonnes of steam per hour (t/h) capacity or units (monthly)
rics.meaning: Monthly production of industrial boilers by enterprises above designated size in Beijing Municipality, the first of two Beijing boiler series. Published by NBS Beijing Bureau, typically released in the second or third week of the following month. Beijing's industrial boiler market is shaped by stringent environmental restrictions — the city has aggressively phased out coal-fired industrial boilers under successive clean-air action plans since 2013.
rics.how_to_use: Beijing boiler output is a policy-sensitive indicator. A sharp production decline signals successful coal boiler retirement and clean-energy substitution — not economic weakness. By contrast, elevated output of natural gas or biomass boilers suggests active replacement cycle demand. Useful for gauging the pace of de-coaling in China's most-watched air quality region; compare with Hebei (aCNCNJWECM) where coal boiler phase-out started later.

rics.how_to_use: Pair with aCNCNAMGMM to capture the full Beijing boiler production profile. Given Beijing's near-complete phase-out of coal industrial boilers by 2020, persistent production here likely reflects gas-fired and electric boilers for district heating and industrial steam applications. Any rebound in boiler output in Beijing likely reflects replacement demand tied to aged district heating infrastructure upgrades, not new capacity addition.

rics.how_to_use: Chongqing boiler output reflects the industrial metabolism of southwest China's largest manufacturing hub. Strong production here correlates with activity at CQRC (Chongqing's chemical complex), Ford/Changan automotive lines, and local steel mills. Compare with the Hubei series (aCNCNHUTGM/aCNCNWZKIM) to assess broader Yangtze River belt industrial momentum. Seasonal peaks typically appear in Q2-Q3 before winter procurement cutoffs.

Fujian's boiler output is closely tied to its petrochemical corridor (Quanzhou, Zhangzhou) and Taiwan-funded electronics and machinery manufacturers. rics.meaning: Monthly production of industrial boilers by enterprises above designated size in Guangdong Province, the first of two Guangdong boiler series. Published by NBS Guangdong Bureau monthly, typically released in the second or third week of the following month. Guangdong's boiler market is driven by the Pearl River Delta manufacturing complex — textiles, food processing, chemical, and electronics factories — one of the world's densest industrial clusters.
rics.how_to_use: Guangdong boiler production is a high-frequency indicator of Pearl River Delta factory activity. The province's strict emission standards (Guangdong has led China in industrial boiler NOx controls) mean production increasingly reflects high-efficiency and low-emission equipment. YoY growth above 10% typically coincides with factory capacity expansion cycles driven by export orders. Compare with Zhejiang (aCNCNYXDIM/aCNCNSQZPM) for coastal manufacturing belt trends.

Published by NBS Guangdong Bureau monthly.
rics.how_to_use: Use in conjunction with aCNCNZICSM to assess the full scope of Guangdong's boiler sector. Guangdong's transition away from coal-fired industrial boilers has been among the fastest in China — the province has targeted complete coal boiler phase-out in key cities by 2025. Therefore, divergence between the two series (if one tracks total output and the other tracks specific fuel-type boilers) reveals the structural energy transition underway in China's largest manufacturing province.

rics.description: Industrial boiler production, Hebei ProvinceYear on Year Growth, Cumulative
rics.subcategory: Industrial Boiler Production — Hebei Province, YoY Growth Cumulative
rics.meaning: Cumulative year-on-year growth rate of industrial boiler production by enterprises above designated size in Hebei Province. Published by NBS Hebei Bureau monthly, typically released in the second or third week of the following month. Hebei surrounds Beijing and is China's most-watched province for industrial emission compliance — it hosts major steel, cement, and coal industries that are the primary boiler end-users.
rics.how_to_use: Hebei boiler production is among the most policy-sensitive in China. Cumulative growth turning sharply negative (e.g., -20% to -40%) during major environmental enforcement campaigns (2017 '散乱污' crackdown, 2021 winter emission controls) confirms compliance-driven demand destruction. A rebound in cumulative growth after enforcement cycles signals replacement-demand for cleaner equipment. Critical context for anticipating Chinese steel and cement sector cost structures.
