rics.subcategory: Industrial Boiler Production — Hebei Province, YoY Growth Current Period
rics.meaning: Current-period (monthly) year-on-year growth rate of industrial boiler production by enterprises above designated size in Hebei Province. Published by NBS Hebei Bureau monthly. Unlike aCNCNJWECM (cumulative), this series captures month-by-month production momentum changes without smoothing from the YTD accumulation effect.
rics.how_to_use: The current-period YoY series is more volatile but faster-reacting than the cumulative series — swings of ±30% month-on-month YoY are common around Chinese New Year or major enforcement policy announcements. Use this for early-cycle detection: three consecutive months of recovering growth after negative prints often mark the turn in Hebei industrial activity. Pair with Tangshan steel mill utilization data for cross-sector validation.

rics.description: Industrial boiler production, Heilongjiang Province
rics.subcategory: Industrial Boiler Production — Heilongjiang Province (Series A)
rics.units: tonnes of steam per hour (t/h) capacity or units (monthly)
rics.meaning: Monthly production of industrial boilers by enterprises above designated size in Heilongjiang Province, the first of two Heilongjiang series. Published by NBS Heilongjiang Bureau monthly, typically in the second or third week of the following month. Heilongjiang is a northeastern rust-belt province with significant coal mining, petrochemical (Daqing oilfield), and grain-processing industries — all major boiler consumers for process heat and power.
rics.how_to_use: Heilongjiang boiler output is a northeast China industrial health indicator. The province's heavy dependence on district heating (극-cold winters, average January -20°C) means boiler production has a pronounced seasonal pattern with Q2-Q3 manufacturing peaks. Structural decline in coal mine operations and petrochemical output in Daqing (declining oilfield) exerts multi-year downward pressure — production running 10-20% below 2015 levels is the new baseline. Compare with Jilin and Liaoning for Northeast rust-belt industrial complex trends.

rics.meaning: Monthly production of industrial boilers by enterprises above designated size in Heilongjiang Province — the second of two Heilongjiang boiler series, likely differentiated by measurement variant (current period vs. cumulative) or product sub-category. Published by NBS Heilongjiang Bureau monthly.
rics.how_to_use: Pair with aCNCNZKQGM for a complete picture of Heilongjiang's boiler manufacturing. Given the province's fiscal stress and SOE restructuring pressures, boiler manufacturers here often face tighter credit conditions than coastal peers — financial costs series (aCNCNQXHN) provide context. Any sustained recovery in Heilongjiang boiler output (two or more quarters of positive YoY) would signal genuine northeast industrial revitalization, a key policy goal under China's '振兴东北' strategy.

rics.description: Industrial boiler production, Henan Province
rics.subcategory: Industrial Boiler Production — Henan Province (Series A)
rics.units: tonnes of steam per hour (t/h) capacity or units (monthly)
rics.meaning: Monthly production of industrial boilers by enterprises above designated size in Henan Province, the first of two Henan boiler series. Henan is China's most populous province and a major industrial hub with significant food processing, aluminum smelting (Zhongyuan Aluminum), and coal chemical industries — all large boiler consumers.
rics.how_to_use: Henan boiler output correlates with provincial FAI in heavy industry — the province hosts some of China's largest aluminum smelters (energy-intensive, requiring massive steam generation). Boiler production YoY growth of 8%+ in Henan often signals fresh aluminum or chemical plant commissioning. Track alongside Henan's electricity consumption and industrial value-added for consistency checks. Environmental compliance crackdowns around Zhengzhou (PM2.5 controls) can create sharp production swings.

rics.meaning: Monthly production of industrial boilers by enterprises above designated size in Henan Province — the second of two Henan series, likely differentiated by measurement period (current period vs. cumulative) or unit basis. Published by NBS Henan Bureau monthly.
rics.how_to_use: Pair with aCNCNPKOXM to construct a complete monthly Henan boiler production profile. Henan has been a priority province for coal boiler replacement under national air quality improvement programs — the province aims to replace over 1 million small coal boilers. This replacement cycle creates replacement demand rather than incremental demand, meaning positive output growth in a declining-coal-share environment reflects the ongoing equipment upgrade wave rather than new industrial capacity.

The COVID-19 lockdown (January-April 2020) caused one of the most dramatic production collapses in this series — useful as a stress-test benchmark. Normal conditions: YoY growth of 5-10% tracks reasonably with provincial industrial value-added. Track alongside Dongfeng Motor production announcements and WISCO utilization rates for sector-specific context.

With Jiangxi's emergence as a lithium battery materials hub (NMC precursors), watch for new demand from battery chemical plants — a structural growth driver for specialized high-pressure boilers.

The province's steel sector (Anshan Steel, Benxi Steel) is the primary boiler demand driver — blast furnace and rolling mill operations require extensive steam generation. Persistent YoY declines (the structural norm since 2014) reflect secular overcapacity and SOE restructuring, not cyclical weakness. Any sustained recovery (+10% for 3+ consecutive months) would be significant policy news.

Xi'an's growing semiconductor and aerospace industries (Aviation Industry Corporation) add a high-tech dimension to boiler demand. Monitor alongside Shaanxi coal output and coal chemical capex data.

Key risk: Shandong's private refinery sector (地炼) is opaque and can distort readings when under regulatory pressure.

rics.description: Industrial capacity utilization, coal mining & washing industry
rics.meaning: Quarterly industrial capacity utilisation rate for the coal mining and washing industry, published by the NBS as part of its quarterly industrial capacity survey. China's coal mining sector had chronic overcapacity through 2015; the 2016 'supply-side reform' (去产能) aimed to eliminate 800 Mt/year of capacity, pushing utilisation rates from ~65% toward ~80%. Current national coal capacity is ~5 billion tonnes/year.
rics.how_to_use: Utilisation below 75% signals latent supply capacity that can be mobilised quickly during price spikes — a ceiling on coal price rallies. Above 85%, the coal market is supply-constrained and spot prices (Qinhuangdao 5,500 kcal thermal coal) will be supported. The series is released quarterly (March, June, September, December data), so use alongside monthly raw coal output (aCNCNKMHRM) as the intra-quarter proxy. A utilisation drop below 70% has historically preceded NBS announcements of further capacity rationalisation programs.

When coated sheet output rises alongside appliance production data (NBS consumer goods index), it confirms consumer sector recovery in China is broad-based. An unusual production surge alongside flat demand may indicate mills are converting commodity HRC to coated grades to improve margins — watch for SHFE coated steel spot premiums over HRC.

rics.subcategory: Electric Power and Heat Power — YoY Output Growth
rics.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of industrial output for electric power and heat power generation and supply. Published monthly by NBS, typically released ~15th of the following month. China's total electricity generation exceeds 8,000 TWh/year (world's largest), with thermal (coal), hydropower, wind, and solar as main sources. District heating is a significant northern China energy segment.
rics.how_to_use: Electric power output growth is the most direct proxy for China's real economy activity — electricity consumption is harder to fake than GDP. Normal range: 4-8% YoY in steady growth; above 10% signals industrial/construction boom; negative growth (COVID-impacted months, policy-directed capacity controls) is a strong recession signal. Cross-check against aCNVAIPELR for series consistency. A 1 ppt change in power output growth historically correlates with roughly 0.3-0.4 ppt change in industrial value-added growth.

For macro model purposes, the electricity output series is a key component of China's 'activity nowcast' — used by Li Keqiang's famous three-indicator index alongside rail freight and bank loans.

rics.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of industrial output for electrical machinery and equipment manufacturing. Published monthly by NBS, typically released ~15th of the following month. China is the world's largest producer of electrical machinery, accounting for ~35% of global output.
rics.how_to_use: Electrical machinery output is the most direct gauge of China's energy transition manufacturing boom — EV battery production, solar inverters, wind generator manufacturing, and HV transformer output all feed into this series. YoY growth above 15% (as seen in 2021-23 when NEV battery output surged) signals strong clean energy capex. CATL's Ningde and Sichuan gigafactories alone contribute materially to monthly swings. Cross-reference with EV production data (CAAM) and solar installation data (NEA) for demand validation.

Significant divergence (>2 ppts) suggests an NBS reclassification — most likely related to the 2017 revision when new energy vehicle batteries were reclassified under electrical machinery. Both series are essential context for Chinese electrical equipment exporters (cables, transformers, motors — major BRI export categories).

rics.description: Production, Electricity, Chg Y/Y

rics.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of industrial value added for electricity production. Industrial value added differs from physical output volume — it measures the net contribution of the electricity production sector to GDP after subtracting intermediate inputs.
rics.how_to_use: Value-added based electricity sector growth is used in national accounts construction and cross-sector comparisons. Typically runs 1-2 ppts below or above physical output growth (aCNPDENH/aCNPDENHC) depending on fuel cost dynamics — when input fuel costs are high relative to tariffs, value-added growth lags physical output growth. The gap between value-added and physical output growth is a real-time profitability signal for the power sector. Critical component of China's secondary industry (工业) GDP calculation.

rics.how_to_use: Sustained growth above +5% YoY in ferrous mining value-added signals domestic Chinese iron ore miners are ramping supply — typically a lagged response to high iron ore prices. China domestic ore (~200 Mt/year of useable iron equivalent) is high-cost (~$80-100/t production cost vs. Australian ~$18-22/t) but provides supply security. When this indicator rises while seaborne prices (Platts 62% Fe) fall, domestic mines are substituting for imports and compressing the price floor.

rics.description: Production, Iron ore
rics.meaning: Monthly raw (run-of-mine) iron ore production in China, published by the NBS. China mines ~1 billion tonnes/year of raw ore, but at very low average iron grades (~25-32% Fe vs. Australian/Brazilian benchmarks at 57-65% Fe), yielding roughly 250 Mt/year of iron units after beneficiation. China's domestic iron ore is the critical swing supply source given the ~$70/t cost premium over seaborne imports.
rics.how_to_use: Raw ore volumes alone are misleading without grade/yield adjustments — 1 Mt of Chinese raw ore contains roughly 0.28 Mt of iron equivalent vs. 0.62 Mt from Australian Pilbara ore. Use in combination with aCNPDFEORG (growth rate) and aCNVAMFMHR (value-added growth) for a triangulated domestic supply assessment. When raw ore production declines >10% YoY for two consecutive months, assume a ~30 Mt/year equivalent seaborne import replacement requirement — a meaningful demand uplift for Australian and Brazilian miners.

This series provides the rate-of-change signal without requiring base-year normalization, making it directly comparable across time periods and useful for momentum analysis.
rics.how_to_use: A sustained deceleration to below -5% YoY growth in domestic iron ore production, when seaborne prices are simultaneously above $100/t, indicates Chinese domestic miners are facing structural (geological or environmental) constraints rather than price-driven curtailment — a bullish seaborne iron ore signal. Conversely, growth above +8% YoY with seaborne prices below $90/t signals Chinese miners are defending market share at marginal cost, capping the upside for Australian/Brazilian iron ore prices.

Metal products (NBS industry C33) includes metal structural components, metal containers, hardware, metal tools, and spring products — all downstream of steel and aluminum primary production, serving construction, auto, machinery, and consumer goods.
rics.how_to_use: Metal products value-added growth is a downstream steel demand quality indicator — it tells you not just whether steel production is rising but whether that steel is being transformed into value-added manufactured products. Growth above +6% YoY in this series alongside flat steel production implies downstream fabrication efficiency gains (yield improvements, product mix upgrading). Cross with aCNVAMETVR (Series B) for data reliability, and use the composite to assess whether China's manufacturing base is moving up the value chain.

rics.description: Production, Metal Products, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of industrial value-added in metal products manufacturing (Series B) — second NBS series for the same sub-sector as aCNVANMETR. The two series may differ in enterprise classification scope (e.g., whether repair services are included), base-year deflation methodology, or data vintage.
rics.how_to_use: Use in tandem with aCNVANMETR as a quality-control pair for the metal products sector. Consistent above-10% growth across both series indicates the downstream steel fabrication sector is in a strong expansion phase — supportive of sustained or growing flat-steel demand (HRC, CRC, coated grades) from structural steel fabricators, auto parts stampers, and equipment manufacturers. Persistent divergence between the two series warrants investigation of methodology changes before using in econometric models.

rics.description: Production, Mobile communication equipment
rics.meaning: Monthly production of mobile communication equipment (primarily smartphones) by industrial enterprises above designated size in China. Published monthly by NBS, typically ~15th of the following month. China produces roughly 1.5-1.8 billion mobile phones per year — approximately 75% of global smartphone supply. Major production concentrated in Guangdong (Foxconn Shenzhen, OPPO, vivo), Chongqing (Foxconn), and Zhengzhou (Foxconn largest iPhone plant globally).
rics.how_to_use: China smartphone production is a direct supply-chain indicator for Apple, Samsung (Korean components), and domestic brands (Xiaomi, OPPO, Huawei, vivo). Normal monthly output: 110-150 million units. A drop below 100 million/month signals either demand weakness or supply disruption (COVID factory lockdowns in Q4 2022 at Zhengzhou were among the most market-impactful disruptions in recent memory). Cross-reference Foxconn Taiwan revenue disclosures and iPhone upgrade cycle calendars for validation.

rics.description: Production, Non-Ferrous Metals Mining and Dressing, Chg Y/Y
rics.subcategory: Non-Ferrous Metals Mining Value-Added Growth (Series A)
rics.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of industrial value-added in the non-ferrous metals mining and dressing sector (Series A), published by the NBS. Covers copper, aluminum (bauxite), lead, zinc, nickel, tin, molybdenum, and rare earth mining and beneficiation at above-designated-size Chinese mining operations — the upstream supply side of China's base metals complex.
rics.how_to_use: A reliable leading indicator for domestic non-ferrous metal supply: growth above +8% YoY implies Chinese miners are aggressively expanding upstream supply, which typically leads to smelter output growth (aCNVAPNMPR) by 3-6 months and ultimately base metal price pressure if not absorbed by demand. When this series contracts during periods of high LME prices, it signals genuine supply constraints at the mining/beneficiation stage — structurally bullish for copper and zinc.

rics.description: Production, Non-Ferrous Metals Mining and Dressing, Chg Y/Y
rics.subcategory: Non-Ferrous Metals Mining Value-Added Growth (Series B)
rics.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of non-ferrous metals mining and dressing value-added (Series B) — second NBS data series complementing aCNVAMNFIR. Covers the same upstream non-ferrous mining sector (copper, lead, zinc, bauxite, rare earths) and may reflect different enterprise coverage, statistical vintage, or cumulative vs. current-period methodology.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-validate with aCNVAMNFIR: if both series are below 0% YoY, the signal is unambiguous — China's upstream non-ferrous mine supply is contracting, providing support for LME base metals prices as concentrate availability tightens. When Series B is growing while Series A is flat or negative, check whether the divergence reflects enterprise scope differences (state-owned vs. all-ownership) before drawing macro conclusions.

rics.description: Production, Non-Metal Minerals Mining and Dressing, Chg Y/Y
rics.subcategory: Non-Metal Minerals Mining Value-Added Growth (Series A)
rics.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of industrial value-added in non-metallic mineral mining and dressing (Series A), published by the NBS. This sector (NBS industry B10-B12) covers limestone, granite, sand/gravel, gypsum, kaolin, phosphate rock, and coal gangue mining — inputs to cement, glass, ceramics, fertiliser, and construction materials industries, all of which are intensive consumers of energy and logistics.
rics.how_to_use: Non-metal minerals mining growth is a leading indicator for cement and construction materials demand — when this series accelerates above +6% YoY, cement producers are drawing down limestone quarry inventories ahead of construction season (March–October). Compare with aCNVAJMMOR (Series B) for triangulation. The construction sector link makes this a secondary indicator for rebar and structural steel demand — expect a 4-8 week lead-lag between non-metal mining acceleration and rebar demand pickup.

rics.description: Production, Non-Metal Minerals Mining and Dressing, Chg Y/Y
rics.subcategory: Non-Metal Minerals Mining Value-Added Growth (Series B)
rics.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of non-metallic mineral mining and dressing value-added (Series B) — second NBS series for the same sector as aCNVAMMOBR. Both cover the quarrying and processing of industrial minerals used in construction (limestone, sand, gravel), chemicals (phosphate, sulfur), and advanced materials (graphite, industrial diamonds, high-purity quartz).
rics.how_to_use: Where aCNVAMMOBR and this series diverge significantly, investigate whether the difference reflects reclassification of enterprises between non-metal mining and non-metal products manufacturing. High-purity quartz and industrial graphite within the non-metal minerals sector are of increasing strategic interest (semiconductor supply chains); a spike in this series alongside rising electronics exports (aCNCEXBA) may reflect graphite electrode or synthetic quartz expansion beyond just construction aggregates.

rics.description: Production, Non-metal mineral products, Chg Y/Y
rics.subcategory: Non-Metal Mineral Products Value-Added Growth (Series A)
rics.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of industrial value-added in the non-metallic mineral products manufacturing sector (Series A), published by the NBS. This sector (NBS industry C30) covers cement, flat glass, ceramics, refractory materials, stone processing, and mineral-wool insulation — all heavily property-construction and infrastructure-linked.
rics.how_to_use: Cement and glass production, which dominate this sector, are the most coincident indicators of China's construction activity. When aCNPMNMMPC falls below -5% YoY for two consecutive months, property new starts are almost certainly in severe contraction — a strong bearish signal for rebar and long steel. The glass component tracks property completion (windows/glazing are installed at near-completion stage) rather than starts, providing a different phase of the construction cycle signal.

rics.description: Production, Non-metal mineral products, Chg Y/Y
rics.subcategory: Non-Metal Mineral Products Value-Added Growth (Series B)
rics.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of non-metallic mineral products manufacturing value-added (Series B) — second NBS series for the same sector as aCNPMNMMPC. Both cover cement, glass, ceramics, and refractory products; methodological differences between the two series are typical of NBS dual-series reporting and may reflect revised industrial census base years.
rics.how_to_use: Use with aCNPMNMMPC as a dual-series cement/glass demand indicator; when both series converge below zero, the confidence level on construction sector contraction is high. The refractory materials sub-component within this sector is directly linked to steel furnace maintenance cycles — rising refractories output (when disaggregated) implies steel mills are rebuilding blast furnace linings, a signal of production restart or capacity expansion intent.

rics.description: Production, Other Mining, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of industrial value-added in other mining sectors (Series A), published by the NBS. 'Other mining' (NBS industry B09 or similar residual category) captures rare earth mining, potash mining, gemstone extraction, and specialty mineral extraction not classified under coal, ferrous, or non-ferrous mining — including China's critical minerals supply chains.
rics.how_to_use: This series is increasingly relevant as a rare earth and critical minerals proxy — China controls ~85% of global rare earth mining and processing, and NBS 'other mining' captures much of this activity. A sustained rise above +10% YoY in this series, concurrent with rare earth export quota announcements, signals China is expanding rare earth capacity ahead of anticipated export controls — the pattern seen in 2023-2024 before tungsten/germanium/gallium restrictions.

rics.description: Production, Other Mining, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of 'other mining' value-added (Series B) — second NBS series complementing aCNVAMOOAR for the residual mining categories beyond coal, ferrous, and non-ferrous metals. Includes rare earth, potash, and specialty mineral extraction; may also capture artisanal gold mining and salt production depending on NBS scope definitions.
rics.how_to_use: Use alongside aCNVAMOOAR for signal reliability on China's critical minerals mining sector. When both 'other mining' series are rising strongly in a period when official export quotas for rare earths (REE) are being tightened, it suggests China is building domestic rare earth stockpiles before restricting exports — historically a precursor to price spikes in terbium, dysprosium, and neodymium markets used in EV motors and wind turbines.

A 10% YoY rise in this series during periods of elevated Brent crude prices (above $80/bbl) is a reliable signal that China's energy sector is ramping drilling capex. rics.description: Production, Pig iron
rics.meaning: Monthly national pig iron production in China, published by the NBS. Pig iron is the molten iron output from blast furnaces (BF), produced at a ~1.1:1 ratio from sinter/pellet iron ore and coke/coal; nearly all of China's ~850-870 Mt/year pig iron is immediately converted to crude steel in BOFs. This series is effectively a real-time blast furnace utilisation indicator.
rics.how_to_use: Pig iron production tracks the BF operating rate (~3,000 blast furnaces in China). Monthly output above 75 Mt implies national BF capacity utilisation above 85% — near full utilisation. A drop of >5 Mt month-on-month typically signals deliberate production cuts (either environmental curtailment orders or mill-level margin-driven shutdowns) and has historically led iron ore futures (DCE i2509) to fall $5-10/t within 2 weeks. Ratio to crude steel (aCNPDCRDS): BF-BOF route should be ~0.83 pig iron/crude steel — divergence signals EAF share shift.

rics.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of industrial value-added in printing and recording media reproduction (Series A), published by the NBS. This sector (NBS industry C23) encompasses commercial printing, books/periodicals printing, and optical media reproduction — it consumes tinplate (ink cans), aluminium printing plates, and specialty paper. Included in the metals/mining batch as part of a broader NBS industrial dataset.
rics.how_to_use: Treat as a cross-sector demand indicator for metallic packaging materials — specifically tinplate (aCNCNAZHXM) and aluminum foil. When printing and media sector value-added decelerates sharply, it signals declining consumption of aluminium printing plates and tinplate ink cans. Use primarily as a benchmark for comparing sector-specific cost trends (aCNCNKYRFM, aCNCNPHJNM) rather than as a standalone metals demand driver.

rics.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of industrial output for railway, shipping, aerospace and other transport equipment manufacturing. Published monthly by NBS, typically ~15th of the following month. Covers CRRC rail rolling stock (world's largest train manufacturer), Jiangnan/COSCO shipbuilding (world #1 shipbuilder), AVIC aircraft, and satellite/space equipment. Driven by domestic rail network expansion and BRI-linked exports.
rics.how_to_use: Transport equipment output growth above 10% YoY signals an active infrastructure investment cycle — China's HSR network expansion (current ~43,000 km) and metro system build-outs drive CRRC order books. Shipbuilding surges (South Korea competition important context) reflect global trade recovery and naval vessel construction. Compare with aCNPDTRNEQ for series consistency. Rail and ship delivery lead times (18-36 months) mean this output series lags order data by 1.5-3 years — use new order data as a forward indicator.

The two series should broadly align — notable divergence may indicate that one includes military/aerospace production classified separately in a revised industrial taxonomy. This sector is particularly relevant for tracking China's naval expansion (Type 075 amphibious assault ships, Type 055 destroyers) and space program (Long March rockets) — both are captured in 'other transport equipment' under NBS classification, adding a defense/space dimension often overlooked in purely commercial analysis.

rics.description: Production, Repair of metal products, machinery and equipment, Chg Y/Y
rics.subcategory: Metal Products & Machinery Repair Value-Added Growth (Series A)
rics.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of industrial value-added in the repair of metal products, machinery, and equipment (Series A), published by the NBS. This sector captures maintenance, overhaul, and refurbishment services for industrial metal products and machinery — a counter-cyclical activity that tends to accelerate when new capex is constrained but operational equipment must be maintained.
rics.how_to_use: Repair sector growth above +10% YoY in a period of declining new-machinery production (aCNCNHAFYM, aCNCNPCIHM) suggests industrial enterprises are extending asset lives rather than investing in new equipment — a typical late-cycle or downturn indicator for metals demand. Conversely, when repair activity and new equipment production both rise simultaneously, it signals a full industrial upcycle where both maintenance backlogs and new capacity are being addressed.

rics.description: Production, Repair of metal products, machinery and equipment, Chg Y/Y

rics.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of metal products and machinery repair value-added (Series B) — second NBS series for the same sub-sector as aCNVALREPR. The repair/maintenance sector for metal equipment is strategically important in China as ageing capital stock in coal mines, steel mills, and metal processing plants requires increasing maintenance intensity.
rics.how_to_use: Use in conjunction with aCNVALREPR for a complete picture of China's industrial maintenance cycle. When repair value-added growth accelerates in sectors like coal mining equipment (cross-check with aCNCNKWDNQ) or steel mill rolls and housings (cross-check with aCNCNPGIUM cast steel), it implies existing capacity is being sweated rather than replaced — supportive of specialty steel and cast steel demand for maintenance applications.

rics.description: Production, Rolled Steel
rics.meaning: Monthly national rolled steel production in China, published by the NBS — the finished steel output indicator, downstream of crude steel (aCNPDCRDS) after hot-rolling, cold-rolling, and forming operations. China produces ~1,300-1,400 Mt/year of rolled products (more than crude steel output because rolling converts some imported semi-finished billets); major product categories include bar/rod, wire, structural sections, sheet/plate, and strip.
rics.how_to_use: Rolled steel production exceeding crude steel (aCNPDCRDS) confirms China is importing semi-finished billets for rolling — check trade data for billet import volumes (HS 7207). The rolled-to-crude ratio persistently above 1.05 is unusual and signals domestic rolling capacity is being run on imported semis. Monthly rolled output above 120 Mt is the 'hot' threshold that typically triggers domestic steel price weakness as finished product supply overwhelms seasonal demand.

rics.description: Production, Rolled steel, plated steel sheet/strip
rics.meaning: Monthly production of rolled steel plated sheet and strip (hot-dip galvanised, electrogalvanised, and tin-plated flat products) in China, published by the NBS with irregular frequency. Plated steel is a premium flat product combining base steel's structural properties with corrosion or aesthetic coatings; consumed in automotive body panels (~30% of demand), white goods, construction roofing, and packaging.
rics.how_to_use: When plated sheet production rises while bare HRC or CRC output is flat, it signals mills are adding coating capacity to capture premium pricing — a margin-improvement strategy typical of steel pricing downturns. Track auto sector production schedules (CAAM monthly auto output data) as the primary demand driver for hot-dip galvanised grades. Plated steel production falling >8% YoY with auto production flat implies coating line maintenance or input (zinc) cost-driven curtailments.

rics.description: Production, Smelting & pressing of ferrous metals, Chg Y/Y
rics.subcategory: Ferrous Metals Smelting & Pressing Value-Added Growth (Series A)
rics.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of industrial value-added in ferrous metals smelting and pressing (Series A), published by the NBS. This sector (NBS industry C31) covers the full steelmaking chain from liquid crude steel through rolling and finishing — the value-added spine of China's steel industry, from Baowu, HBIS, Shagang, Ansteel, and ~200 other significant producers.
rics.how_to_use: This is the most comprehensive value-added indicator for China's steel industry — it captures the entire BF-BOF-rolling chain rather than just crude steel volumes (aCNPDCRDS). When this growth rate exceeds crude steel volume growth, it signals product mix upgrading (more high-value specialty/flat products) or efficiency gains — both bullish for steel sector margins. Growth below -3% YoY while crude steel volumes are flat implies pricing/margin collapse — typical of 2015-2016 style overcapacity crises.

rics.description: Production, Smelting & pressing of ferrous metals, Chg Y/Y
rics.subcategory: Ferrous Metals Smelting & Pressing Value-Added Growth (Series B)
rics.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of ferrous metals smelting and pressing value-added (Series B) — second NBS series for the same steelmaking sector as aCNPSNPF. As with other dual NBS series, differences may arise from enterprise classification scope, base-year methodology, or cumulative vs. current-period calculation approaches in the NBS's industrial census and annual survey reconciliation process.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-validate with aCNPSNPF: when both series are below -5% YoY, the ferrous metals value chain is clearly under severe margin pressure — a systemic signal rather than measurement noise. The dual-series approach is especially important during NBS rebasing years (2015, 2019) when methodological changes can temporarily create large apparent divergences. Strong convergence between Series A and B above +5% YoY is the most reliable green light for overweight Chinese steel sector positions.

rics.description: Production, Smelting and Pressing of Non-Ferrous Metals, Chg Y/Y
rics.subcategory: Non-Ferrous Metals Smelting & Pressing Value-Added Growth (Series A)
rics.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of industrial value-added in non-ferrous metals smelting and pressing (Series A), published by the NBS. This sector (NBS industry C32) covers the smelting and refining of copper, aluminum, lead, zinc, nickel, tin, and precious metals, plus the downstream rolling and forming of these metals into sheets, rods, wires, and profiles. China dominates this sector globally (~55% of world non-ferrous smelting capacity).
rics.how_to_use: This is THE top-level value-added indicator for China's non-ferrous sector — a primary input for global base metals demand models. Growth above +6% YoY signals China's non-ferrous supply chain is expanding production faster than domestic demand, typically an LME price headwind. Cross-check with LME inventory builds: rising aCNVAPNMPR + rising LME stocks is the most bearish combination for base metals. Cross with aCNCNDQMEM (copper) and aCNCNKRWSM (alumina) to decompose by metal.

rics.description: Production, Smelting and Pressing of Non-Ferrous Metals, Chg Y/Y
rics.subcategory: Non-Ferrous Metals Smelting & Pressing Value-Added Growth (Series B)
rics.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of non-ferrous metals smelting and pressing value-added (Series B) — second NBS series complementing aCNVAPNMPR for the same sector. This series may use different enterprise classification, an alternative price deflator, or a different statistical base year compared to Series A, producing the characteristic NBS dual-series divergence pattern.
rics.how_to_use: Use alongside aCNVAPNMPR as a signal quality checker for China's non-ferrous metals sector. Persistent divergence between the two series typically indicates an NBS rebasing event — the NBS revises its industrial census base approximately every 5 years (2015, 2020), creating temporary measurement inconsistencies. Both series contracting below -4% YoY simultaneously is the cleanest signal of a genuine Chinese non-ferrous metals industry downturn — relevant for global copper, aluminum, and zinc price outlooks.

rics.description: Production, Special Purpose Equipment Manufacturing, Chg Y/Y
rics.subcategory: Special Purpose Equipment Manufacturing — YoY Output Growth
rics.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of industrial output for special purpose equipment manufacturing. Published monthly by NBS, typically ~15th of the following month. Special purpose equipment includes mining machinery, metallurgical equipment, construction machinery (XCMG, Sany, Zoomlion, LGMG), agricultural machinery (LOVOL, YANMAR China), and environmental protection/pollution control equipment. China leads globally in construction machinery production.
rics.how_to_use: Special equipment output is the most direct proxy for China's infrastructure investment cycle. Growth above 12% YoY typically coincides with FAI in infrastructure above 5% YoY; contraction below -5% signals capex slump. Excavator monthly sales (CCMA, typically 15,000-25,000 units in upcycle, 8,000-12,000 in downcycle) correlate closely. Environmental equipment sub-segment (wastewater treatment, air pollution control) shows secular growth regardless of the broader construction cycle — driven by $400B+ environmental compliance spending since 2013.

rics.description: Production, Special purpose machinery, Chg Y/Y
rics.subcategory: Special Purpose Machinery — YoY Output Growth
rics.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of industrial output for special purpose machinery — an alternative or related series to aCNVASPEOR, potentially reflecting a different aggregation scope or classification vintage. Published monthly by NBS. May distinguish 'special purpose machinery' (专用设备) from the broader 'special purpose equipment manufacturing' (专用设备制造业) at different levels of the NBS industry taxonomy.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-reference aCNVAFSPER against aCNVASPEOR to identify any scope difference. In NBS taxonomy, 专用设备 is used at different hierarchy levels; the series capturing the more granular sub-category (e.g., excluding environmental machinery) may show different cyclical behavior. When aCNVAFSPER consistently outpaces aCNVASPEOR, it suggests that a specific high-growth sub-segment (e.g., semiconductor equipment, medical devices, or agricultural machinery) is driving the aggregate, while environmental equipment may be relatively weaker.

rics.description: Production, Support activities of mining, Chg Y/Y
rics.subcategory: Mining Support Activities Value-Added Growth (Series A)
rics.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of industrial value-added in support activities for mining (Series A), published by the NBS. Mining support services (NBS industry B11 or equivalent) include mine drilling, blasting, mine shaft sinking, mine dewatering, and mining equipment rental — services intensive in specialty steel (drill pipe, casing, drill bits), explosives, and advanced machinery.
rics.how_to_use: Mining support services act as a leading indicator for future mining production volume: when support activity accelerates 3-6 months ahead of actual output data, it confirms new mine capacity is being prepared for commissioning. Growth above +15% YoY in this series alongside strong non-ferrous mining confidence (aCNCNADZYQ) signals a significant capacity expansion cycle is underway — typically translates into supply pressure for target metals 12-18 months later.

rics.description: Production, Support activities of mining, Chg Y/Y
rics.subcategory: Mining Support Activities Value-Added Growth (Series B)
rics.meaning: Monthly year-on-year growth rate of mining support activities value-added (Series B) — second NBS series for the same sector as aCNVALSUMR. Both series track the service sector surrounding China's mining industry: drilling contractors, blasting specialists, mine ventilation engineers, and mining software providers — all of which respond to upstream mining capex cycles.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-validate with aCNVALSUMR: dual-series confirmation of above-10% YoY growth in mining support activities indicates the mining industry is at the peak of a capital deployment cycle. When both support series contract simultaneously with raw material prices (aCNCNNFMEM, aCNPPIAR) still elevated, it signals mine operators are cutting capex while hoping to hold output — a recipe for future supply shortfall and price recovery 12-24 months ahead.

rics.description: Production, Thick steel plate
rics.meaning: Monthly production of thick steel plate (heavy plate, typically >8 mm gauge hot-rolled flat steel) in China, published by the NBS with irregular frequency. Thick plate is a capital-intensive specialty flat product consumed in shipbuilding (~35% of demand), bridges and large steel structures, pressure vessels (boilers, chemical reactors), offshore platforms, and heavy machinery. China is the world's largest thick plate producer (~25 Mt/year).
rics.how_to_use: Thick plate production is the primary shipbuilding and heavy engineering cycle indicator in China's steel data. When production rises >10% YoY alongside strong civil steel ship output (aCNCNZGMEM), it confirms a genuine shipbuilding super-cycle rather than a temporary scheduling effect. Korean and Japanese shipyards also consume Chinese thick plate — monitor export steel flows alongside domestic production for the split between domestic and export-driven demand.

rics.description: Production, automotive equipment
rics.meaning: Monthly production of automotive equipment (manufacturing machinery and tooling for vehicle production lines) by industrial enterprises above designated size. Published monthly by NBS, typically released ~15th of the following month. Covers stamping presses, welding robots, painting equipment, assembly-line conveyor systems, and body-in-white production equipment used in auto assembly plants.
rics.how_to_use: Automotive equipment production is a capital expenditure indicator for China's car manufacturing industry — an active production line retooling wave for EV platforms generates significant equipment orders. Typically, automotive equipment output spikes 18-24 months ahead of new model launch cycles. Chinese EV brands (BYD, NIO, Li Auto, AITO) all completed major plant expansions in 2022-24, driving a multi-year equipment investment cycle. Compare with aCNPDAUMOT for the paired automotive equipment series and cross-reference with CAAM vehicle production data.

rics.description: Production, cement special equipment, Anhui Province
rics.subcategory: Cement Special Equipment Output — Anhui Province
rics.meaning: Monthly production of cement special equipment (kilns, mills, separators, conveyor systems for cement plants) by enterprises above designated size in Anhui Province. Published by NBS Anhui Bureau monthly, typically in the second or third week of the following month. Anhui hosts major cement equipment manufacturers, connected to the province's large cement and construction materials industry (Conch Cement, China's largest cement producer, is Anhui-headquartered).
rics.how_to_use: Cement equipment output from Anhui is directly linked to Conch Cement's domestic capacity expansion and BRI-linked cement plant exports. China has exported cement plant turnkey projects to Africa, Southeast Asia, and South Asia — Anhui manufacturers are major suppliers. Growth of 15%+ YoY in cement equipment typically precedes global cement production capacity additions by 12-18 months. Decline in output signals either domestic overcapacity rationalization or BRI project pipeline slowdown.

rics.description: Production, civil steel ship
rics.units: DWT (deadweight tonnes) or Number of vessels
rics.meaning: Monthly production of civil steel ships in China, published by the NBS. China has been the world's largest shipbuilder since 2010 (~50% global market share in DWT, ~60% in orders in 2023-2024); major yards include CSSC (China State Shipbuilding Corp), CSIC, Yangzijiang Shipbuilding, and Cosco Shipping Heavy Industry. A civil steel ship is one of the most steel-intensive manufactured goods (~15-20 kt of steel per Capesize bulk carrier).
rics.how_to_use: Ship production is the anchor demand driver for thick plate (aCNPDTHSTP) and medium/heavy structural steel. The current 2023-2025 shipbuilding boom (driven by LNG vessel orders, container replacement, and green-shipping regulations) is a multi-year thick plate demand uplift — sustaining high production figures here for 3+ consecutive years is a structural bullish signal for shipbuilding steel grades. Cross with order book data (Clarksons Research): a ratio of order book/deliveries above 3 years confirms sustained forward demand.

rics.description: Production, concrete machinery, Industrial Production & Utilization, Monthly, National Bureau of Statistics of China
rics.meaning: Year-on-year growth rate of concrete machinery production (concrete mixers, pump trucks, batching plants, and transit mixers) by industrial enterprises above designated size. Published monthly by NBS, typically released ~15th of the following month. China's concrete machinery sector is led by SANY, Zoomlion, and XCMG — globally dominant producers that export to over 100 countries.
rics.how_to_use: Concrete machinery output growth is one of the most reliable leading indicators for China's fixed asset investment in construction. Growth above 15% YoY typically precedes a construction boom by 3-6 months; decline below -10% signals cement demand contraction 2-3 months ahead. SANY's monthly mixer truck sales data (reported independently) provides weekly cross-check. The 2021 construction machinery super-cycle saw growth peak above 50% YoY; the 2022-23 downturn saw -30% prints — an extreme range that mirrors real estate sector volatility directly.

rics.description: Production, concrete machinery, Volume, Industrial Production & Utilization, Monthly, National Bureau of Statistics of China
rics.meaning: Monthly production volume (absolute level) of concrete machinery (concrete mixers, pump trucks, batching plants) by industrial enterprises above designated size. Published monthly by NBS. This is the levels companion to aCNCNDXHEM (which shows the YoY growth rate), allowing calculation of absolute production scale rather than just the rate of change.
rics.how_to_use: Use the absolute production level to construct longer-run trend analysis and identify where the current cycle sits relative to peak production. Peak monthly concrete machinery output reached ~25,000-30,000 units in the 2020-21 super-cycle; a structural level of 15,000-20,000 units represents the 'new normal' given property sector deleveraging. The level series also enables comparison of China's production share of global concrete equipment — China typically accounts for 40-50% of global concrete mixer output. Combine with aCNCNDXHEM for a complete picture.

rics.description: Production, cotton processing machinery
rics.meaning: Monthly production of cotton processing machinery (ginning machines, carding machines, spinning frames, weaving looms for cotton textile processing) by industrial enterprises above designated size. Published monthly by NBS, typically released ~15th of the following month. China's cotton textile machinery sector is concentrated in Jiangsu (Jintan, Wuxi machinery clusters), Henan, and Xinjiang — the latter as China's largest cotton-growing region.
rics.how_to_use: Cotton processing machinery output correlates with textile industry capex cycles and reflects cotton production volumes (Xinjiang accounts for ~85% of Chinese cotton). Equipment output surges often accompany new Xinjiang cotton processing capacity additions — geopolitically sensitive given international scrutiny. Cross-reference with Xinjiang cotton planting area (NBS agricultural data) and global cotton prices (ICE). A secondary market is the aftermarket replacement cycle for older machinery, driven by productivity upgrade pressure from rising labor costs.

rics.description: Production, electric hand tool, Zhejiang Province
rics.subcategory: Electric Hand Tool Production — Zhejiang Province
rics.meaning: Monthly production of electric hand tools (drills, grinders, saws, sanders, and jigsaws) by enterprises above designated size in Zhejiang Province. Published by NBS Zhejiang Bureau monthly, typically in the second or third week of the following month. Zhejiang dominates China's electric hand tool industry — the Jinhua/Yongkang cluster is known as 'China's hardware city,' housing thousands of electric tool manufacturers, many of which export under Western OEM brands (Black & Decker, Bosch have supply chains here).
rics.how_to_use: Zhejiang electric hand tool output is a direct proxy for global DIY and professional tool demand — typically 80%+ of output is for export, making this series highly correlated with Western consumer home improvement cycles. The 2020-21 pandemic-era home improvement surge drove Zhejiang tool output to record highs (+30-40% YoY). Monitor alongside USD/CNY exchange rates and Western retail construction indicators (US housing starts, Europe DIY retail sales) for export order context. Cross-reference with Zhejiang electrical equipment output (aCNCNZWAVM).

rics.description: Production, electrical equipment, Hunan Province
rics.meaning: Monthly production of electrical equipment by enterprises above designated size in Hunan Province. Published by NBS Hunan Bureau monthly, typically in the second or third week of the following month. Hunan's electrical equipment sector includes transmission and distribution equipment (Xuji Electric, Changsha Electric), plus industrial motors and control systems serving the province's diversified manufacturing base (construction machinery, non-ferrous metals, rail equipment).
rics.how_to_use: Hunan electrical equipment output is a regional indicator for central China's electricity infrastructure investment — T&D equipment production typically tracks State Grid/China Southern Grid capex with a 6-12 month lead. The province's special position as home to CRRC's train manufacturing and Sany's construction machinery means electrical equipment demand spans traction motors, inverters, and grid-scale storage equipment. YoY growth above 12% signals active power grid upgrading cycles. Cross-reference with aCNCNZWAVM (Zhejiang) for coastal-inland electrical equipment comparison.

rics.description: Production, electrical equipment, Zhejiang Province
rics.meaning: Monthly production of electrical equipment by enterprises above designated size in Zhejiang Province. Published by NBS Zhejiang Bureau monthly, typically in the second or third week of the following month. Zhejiang is China's third-largest electrical equipment production base after Guangdong and Jiangsu — the Wenzhou and Hangzhou clusters produce low-voltage switchgear, connectors, circuit breakers, and power tools, with a very high export orientation.
rics.how_to_use: Zhejiang electrical equipment output is a high-frequency proxy for global electrical infrastructure demand — Zhejiang manufacturers supply OEM components to Schneider, ABB, Siemens distribution-level equipment. Growth above 15% YoY typically coincides with global grid investment upcycles (the 2021-24 energy transition investment wave drove exceptional Zhejiang output expansion). Cross-reference with Hunan (aCNCNWGBGM) to compare export-oriented Zhejiang vs. domestically-oriented Hunan. Closely linked to electrical export revenue (aCNCEXBA).

rics.description: Production, machine paper & paperboard (except base paper processing)
rics.meaning: Monthly production of machine-made paper and paperboard (excluding base paper processing/converting) by industrial enterprises above designated size nationally. Published monthly by NBS, typically released ~15th of the following month. China is the world's largest paper and paperboard producer (~120 million tonnes/year), with packaging paper (9 Dragon Paper, Lee & Man Paper) dominating output, followed by cultural paper and newsprint.
rics.how_to_use: Machine-made paper output is a leading indicator for packaging and consumer goods activity — China's packaging paper demand closely tracks e-commerce (Alibaba, JD.com) box shipments and industrial goods export packaging. Production surges above 8% YoY typically accompany e-commerce seasonal peaks (Singles' Day in November). Domestic wastepaper recycled fiber costs (after China's 2017-2018 waste paper import ban) make domestic production economics unique — cross-reference with domestic recovered fiber prices for margin context.

rics.description: Production, machine paper & paperboard (except base paper processing), Henan Province
rics.subcategory: Machine-Made Paper & Paperboard Production — Henan Province
rics.meaning: Monthly production of machine-made paper and paperboard (excluding base paper processing) by enterprises above designated size in Henan Province. Published by NBS Henan Bureau monthly, typically in the second or third week of the following month. Henan has developed a significant paper production capacity oriented toward packaging paper and cultural paper for central China's market, utilizing both recycled and virgin fiber inputs.
rics.how_to_use: Henan paper output reflects inland China packaging demand and construction-related paper (cement bags, gypsum board facing) activity — both linked to central China's real estate and logistics sectors. Deceleration below -5% YoY in Henan paper production often coincides with regional real estate or industrial slowdowns. Compare with national series (aCNCNOSHVM) to assess Henan's market share trends — Henan has been expanding paper capacity at the expense of coastal provinces where environmental compliance costs are higher.

rics.description: Production, powder metallurgy parts
rics.meaning: Monthly production of powder metallurgy (PM) parts in China, published by the NBS. PM parts (produced by compacting and sintering metal powders — iron, copper, aluminum, tungsten, stainless) are precision components used in auto transmissions, electric motors, VVT systems, and electronics; China is the world's fastest-growing PM market, consuming ~150,000 tonnes/year of PM iron powders.
rics.how_to_use: PM parts production is an advanced manufacturing metals indicator — rising output signals strength in high-value-added auto components and precision engineering, which consume specialty iron powders, copper powders, and tungsten carbide. The EV transition is a structural tailwind (EV motors use more PM sintered components than ICE transmissions). Cross with aCNCNHAFYM (casting machinery) to assess whether PM is gaining share vs. traditional casting in auto components — a technology shift indicator.

rics.description: Production, power station boiler
rics.units: tonnes of steam per hour (t/h) capacity (monthly)
rics.meaning: Monthly production of power station boilers (utility-scale steam generators for coal/gas/biomass power plants) by industrial enterprises above designated size in China. Published monthly by NBS, typically ~15th of the following month. China's dominant power station boiler manufacturers are Dongfang Boiler (Dongfang Electric Group), Shanghai Boiler Works (Shanghai Electric), and Harbin Boiler Company (Harbin Electric International), which together supply nearly all of China's new coal and biomass power plant boilers and export to BRI countries.
rics.how_to_use: Power station boiler production is the single best indicator of Chinese thermal power capacity pipeline. Monthly production of 100,000+ t/h capacity signals an active coal plant construction wave; sub-60,000 t/h reflects the phase-down of coal capacity addition. However, biomass and gas boiler orders are partially offsetting coal decline — examine the fuel-type breakdown where available. Lead time for delivery is 12-18 months after order; compare with NEA thermal power capacity additions ~18 months later. Critical for China coal demand 2-3 year outlook.

rics.description: Production, turbine generator
rics.meaning: Monthly production of turbine generators (steam turbine generators for coal/gas/nuclear power plants and wind turbine generators) by industrial enterprises above designated size. Published monthly by NBS, typically ~15th of the following month. China's turbine generator manufacturers — Dongfang Turbine, Shanghai Turbine (Shanghai Electric), and Harbin Turbine (Harbin Electric) — are among the world's largest, supplying both domestic power plants and exporting under BRI infrastructure contracts.
rics.how_to_use: Turbine generator production above 15 million kW/month signals robust power capacity build-out pipeline — the 2023-24 period saw exceptionally high output as China added ~220 GW of new power capacity per year. The shift from coal to wind turbine generators within this series is a key structural trend — wind generator capacity growth of 30%+ YoY reflects China's target of 1,200 GW wind+solar by 2030. Cross-reference with power station boiler output (aCNCNOJFMM) — both should track each other in coal plant cycles; divergence indicates rapid growth in non-thermal generation.

rics.description: Production, welding machine
rics.meaning: Monthly production of welding machines (arc welding, MIG/MAG welding, laser welding, and spot welding equipment) by industrial enterprises above designated size. Published monthly by NBS, typically ~15th of the following month. China is the world's largest producer and consumer of welding equipment, with production concentrated in Shanghai, Tianjin, Chengdu, and Guangzhou. Key manufacturers include Lincoln Electric China, Miller China, and domestic brands like Riland, Jasic Technology.
rics.how_to_use: Welding machine production is a broad manufacturing capex indicator — nearly every metal fabrication, shipbuilding, automotive, and construction steel industry requires welding equipment. YoY growth above 10% signals healthy manufacturing investment; decline below -10% reflects capex contraction. The shift from traditional arc welders to robotic laser welding systems (a high-value segment) is a structural upgrade trend — monitor alongside industrial robot installations (CRIA data, ~270k units/year) for the automation investment context. Exports are significant (~30-40% of production).

rics.description: Profit, industrial companies above designated size, entertainment boat & sport boat manufacturing
rics.meaning: Industrial: Profit, industrial companies above designated size, entertainment boat & sport boat manufacturing. Profit statistics for above-designated-size industrial firms — released monthly by NBS.
rics.how_to_use: Industrial profits are the corporate-earnings cycle proxy for China. PPI deflation 2023-24 has compressed industrial-sector margins; profit YoY growth often negative. Watch alongside SOE vs private firm profit splits.

rics.description: Profit, industrial companies above designated size, non-ferrous metal casting
rics.meaning: Profit of industrial companies above designated size in non-ferrous metal casting, published by the NBS with irregular frequency. Non-ferrous casting (aluminum die-casting, copper casting, zinc die-casting) is a downstream processing sector bridging primary metals and component manufacturing; major customers are auto OEMs, electronics assemblers, and construction hardware manufacturers.
rics.how_to_use: Irregular frequency limits time-series analysis — treat as periodic profitability snapshots. When non-ferrous casting profits are strong alongside rising aluminum production (aCNCNDRRM1, aCNCNTPTOM), it confirms healthy downstream margins in the aluminum-to-casting value chain — a positive for aluminum smelter demand. Profit margin compression in casting (cross with aCNCNLOFHM) typically precedes destocking of aluminum ingot by die-casters and a weakening in premium aluminum alloy prices.

rics.description: Raw coal production
rics.meaning: Monthly raw coal (run-of-mine coal) production in China, published by the NBS — China's headline coal output indicator. China produces ~4.5 billion tonnes/year (~53% of global coal output), making it by far the world's largest coal producer; major provinces are Inner Mongolia (~1.1 Bt), Shanxi (~1.3 Bt), and Shaanxi (~700 Mt). Released monthly around the 15th of the following month.
rics.how_to_use: Monthly output above 400 Mt signals China is running at near-maximum mine capacity — typically reached during winter heating demand peaks (Nov–Feb) or government energy security campaigns. A sustained drop below 360 Mt/month is structurally bearish for thermal coal seaborne prices (Newcastle API4) as it implies Chinese domestic supply is constraining and import demand rises. Cross with aCNVAUMWSR (coal value-added growth) and aCNCNKWDNQ (capacity utilisation) for a triangulated coal supply health check.

rics.description: Sales cost, industrial companies above designated size, medical diagnostic, monitoring & treatment equipment manufacturing
rics.subcategory: Medical Diagnostic, Monitoring & Treatment Equipment — Sales Cost
rics.meaning: Sales cost (cost of goods sold relating to sales revenue) for industrial companies above designated size in the medical diagnostic, monitoring and treatment equipment manufacturing sub-sector. Published by NBS as part of Industrial Enterprise Financial Statistics; frequency is irregular given the blank field. Covers makers of CT scanners, MRI systems, ultrasound devices, patient monitors, and radiotherapy equipment — a sector dominated by Mindray, United Imaging, and joint-venture multinationals.
rics.how_to_use: Medical equipment sales cost evolution reveals margin dynamics — sustained cost growth outpacing revenue growth implies margin compression, often driven by component inflation (semiconductors, rare earth magnets in MRI machines) or competitive pricing pressure. China's medical equipment sector has seen rapid domestic brand market share gains (Mindray winning domestic hospital tenders previously dominated by GE, Philips, Siemens). Compare with equipment export data (aCNCEXBA) to assess whether domestic cost efficiency translates into export competitiveness gains.

rics.description: Sales cost, state-owned industrial companies above designated size, electricity supply
rics.subcategory: State-Owned Industrial Firms — Electricity Supply Sales Cost
rics.meaning: Sales cost for state-owned industrial companies above designated size in the electricity supply (distribution and retail) sector. Published by NBS as part of Industrial Enterprise Financial Statistics; frequency is irregular given the blank field. Captures the cost structure of State Grid Corporation of China (SGCC) and China Southern Power Grid (CSG) — the world's two largest electricity distributors — plus provincial grid companies.
rics.how_to_use: State-owned electricity supply sales costs are dominated by purchased electricity costs (from generators) and transmission/distribution infrastructure expenses. This series is critical for analyzing China's electricity sector value chain — when generator tariffs rise faster than retail tariffs (regulated), state grid distribution costs compress margins. Cross-reference with aCNCNFBSKM (utility profit margins) and aCNCNFYFH (state-owned generation sales value) to construct a full power sector P&L picture. Policy implications: persistent cost increases here drive annual tariff review cycles at NDRC.

rics.description: Steel production, Fujian Province[e]
rics.meaning: Monthly steel production in Fujian Province, published by the NBS Fujian Bureau with irregular frequency (marked [e] — estimated/unofficial). Fujian (~10 Mt/year steel capacity) hosts Sanming Iron and Steel and several smaller mills; the province's steel sector serves local construction and the growing semiconductor/electronics manufacturing base around Fuzhou and Quanzhou.
rics.how_to_use: The [e] flag means use as a directional indicator only — data is less reliable than core provincial series. Fujian steel is increasingly significant as a stainless and specialty steel province (serving semiconductor fab equipment and precision manufacturing). Cross with aCNCNIYVNM (Fujian aluminum) to assess whether the province's industrial metals complex is uniformly expanding or experiencing sector-specific patterns. Irregular frequency means quarterly interpolation may be needed for consistent time-series modeling.

rics.description: Steel production, Gansu Province, Current Period
rics.meaning: Monthly current-period steel production in Gansu Province, published by the NBS Gansu Bureau. Gansu (~5 Mt/year steel capacity) is a northwest China steel producer, anchored by Jiuquan Iron and Steel (JISCO) — one of China's oldest integrated steel enterprises (est. 1958) located near Jiayuguan in the Hexi Corridor. JISCO specialises in plates and structural sections for northwest infrastructure.
rics.how_to_use: Gansu steel is primarily a northwest infrastructure demand indicator and JISCO operational health proxy. JISCO has historically been a financially stressed SOE (requiring restructuring in 2016), so output fluctuations here often reflect balance sheet constraints rather than pure demand signals. When Gansu steel production recovers following a multi-month decline, check whether it coincides with debt restructuring announcements or government capital injections into JISCO.

rics.description: Steel production, Guangdong Province
rics.meaning: Monthly steel (all grades, total finished steel) production in Guangdong Province, as distinct from aCNCNLEGIM which specifically measures crude steel. This series captures the downstream rolled and finished steel picture in Guangdong, including a significant contribution from Zhanjiang's Baowu stainless/silicon steel complex and numerous coastal rolling mills that process semi-finished billets imported from third provinces or overseas.
rics.how_to_use: Compare with aCNCNLEGIM (Guangdong crude steel) to derive Guangdong's implied rolling conversion ratio — when total steel grows faster than crude steel, the province is importing and processing semi-finished billets. A persistent rolling/crude ratio above 1.15 in Guangdong signals strong coastal trading-mill activity — these mills are price-sensitive and will cut when HRC-billet spreads compress below ~CNY 100/t.

rics.description: Steel production, Hebei ProvinceCurrent Period
rics.meaning: Monthly current-period steel production in Hebei Province — China's largest steel-producing province (~240 Mt/year, ~24% of national output) published by the NBS Hebei Bureau. Hebei's steel belt (Tangshan, Handan, Shijiazhuang) is home to HBIS Group (Hesteel), Tangshan Guofeng, Delong Steel, Jingye Group, and hundreds of smaller mills. Tangshan alone produces ~85-90 Mt/year.
rics.how_to_use: This is the single most important provincial steel series in China — Hebei's output alone exceeds the entire production of the US, EU, or Japan. A Hebei 'blast furnace halt' notice from local government (triggered by air quality alerts — common in autumn/winter) cuts Chinese steel production by ~3-5 Mt/week and is the most frequent short-term steel supply shock. Tangshan pollution curtailment orders (Orange/Red alerts) typically follow within 5 days of this series printing above 20 Mt/month.

rics.description: Steel production, Heilongjiang Province, Industrial Production & Utilization, Monthly, National Bureau of Statistics of China
rics.meaning: Monthly steel production in Heilongjiang Province (Series A), published by the NBS Heilongjiang Bureau. This series (alongside aCNCNASSOM) represents Heilongjiang's total steel output including finished rolled products, as opposed to aCNCNIAVM which specifically tracks crude steel. The northeast's steel sector has been in structural decline since the early 2010s, with capacity rationalization ongoing.
rics.how_to_use: Use as a northeast China industrial recovery tracker — when this series stabilises or recovers after multi-year decline, cross-check with NBS northeast revitalisation policy announcements and Heilongjiang SOE credit conditions. Compare the ratio of this series (total steel) to aCNCNIAVM (crude steel) to derive rolling mill efficiency: a rising ratio indicates improving downstream processing activity even as crude steel flatlines, suggesting recovery is starting in fabrication before reaching primary steelmaking.

rics.description: Steel production, Heilongjiang Province, Volume, Industrial Production & Utilization, Monthly, National Bureau of Statistics of China
rics.subcategory: Steel Production — Heilongjiang Province (Series B, Volume)
rics.meaning: Monthly steel production in Heilongjiang Province (Series B — Volume series), published by the NBS Heilongjiang Bureau alongside aCNCNDNCXM. The 'Volume' designation distinguishes this series from potential value-based or index-form presentations of the same underlying data. Together, the two Heilongjiang steel series provide cross-validation for the province's industrial output reporting.
rics.how_to_use: Where aCNCNDNCXM and aCNCNASSOM diverge by >5%, investigate whether the difference reflects different product scope (crude vs. rolled, or all-steel vs. specific grades) rather than measurement error. Both series declining below -10% YoY simultaneously confirms Heilongjiang's steel sector is in genuine contraction — at this point, the macro story is about SOE credit risk (Heilongjiang province debt) rather than physical steel supply, and the policy response typically involves Northeastern Revitalisation Fund disbursements.

rics.description: Steel production, Henan Province
rics.meaning: Monthly steel (total rolled/finished) production in Henan Province, published by the NBS Henan Bureau, as distinct from aCNCNBYBM (Henan crude steel). Henan's steel sector produces both long products (rebar, wire rod) for the province's massive construction market and flat products for its growing auto manufacturing cluster around Zhengzhou (BYD new plant, Foxconn iPad plant nearby).
rics.how_to_use: Compare with aCNCNBYBM (Henan crude steel) to compute the crude-to-finished ratio: a rising ratio above 1.05 indicates Henan mills are processing imported semi-finished billets. Henan's rebar demand is a direct proxy for central China property construction health — when Henan rebar-type output falls >12% YoY, it implies property new starts in this 100M-population province are severely depressed, confirming national housing market stress beyond coastal markets.

rics.description: Steel production, Jiangsu Province, Current Period
rics.meaning: Monthly current-period steel production in Jiangsu Province, published by the NBS Jiangsu Bureau. Jiangsu (~140 Mt/year steel capacity) is China's second-largest steel-producing province after Hebei, anchored by Shagang Group (the world's largest private steel company, ~45 Mt/year), Nanjing Iron and Steel (Baowu subsidiary), and Xingcheng Special Steel. Jiangsu is China's leading specialty steel and flat products hub.
rics.how_to_use: Jiangsu steel is the private-sector-led, export-oriented contrast to state-dominated Hebei: Shagang produces primarily HRC, wire rod, and semi-finished billets for both domestic and export markets. When Jiangsu output rises faster than Hebei (aCNCNLQBDM), it typically signals export-driven demand growth for flat products rather than domestic property-led rebar demand. Monthly output above 12 Mt from Jiangsu indicates Shagang and peers are running at near-full capacity.

rics.description: Steel production, Liaoning Province
rics.meaning: Monthly total steel production in Liaoning Province, published by the NBS Liaoning Bureau, complementing aCNCNBUCLM (Liaoning crude steel). Liaoning's total steel production (including finished rolling) exceeds crude steel volumes when the province's numerous downstream pipe mills, tube mills, and section mills are running at capacity. Key producers: Ansteel, Benxi Steel, Fushun Special Steel, Dalian Steel.
rics.how_to_use: Compare with aCNCNBUCLM (Liaoning crude steel) to assess rolling mill utilisation — total steel consistently above crude steel by >8% indicates active downstream processing and likely billet imports into Liaoning's coastal mills. Liaoning's Dalian port is China's primary seamless pipe export hub — when Liaoning total steel rises faster than crude steel, it often signals strong energy-sector tubular demand (CNPC, Sinopec drilling programmes) feeding through the Dalian pipe cluster.

rics.description: Steel production, Shandong Province, Current Period
rics.meaning: Monthly current-period steel production in Shandong Province, published by the NBS Shandong Bureau. Shandong (~80 Mt/year steel capacity) is China's fourth-largest steel-producing province, with a diverse mix of producers including Shandong Iron and Steel Group (Laiwu + Jinan mills), Rizhao Steel (world's largest single-site steel complex), and numerous coastal rolling mills. Shandong steel feeds the province's giant construction, machinery, and marine equipment sectors.
rics.how_to_use: Shandong's Rizhao mill is one of the world's most efficient integrated steel plants (~25 Mt/year) and a benchmark for coastal seaborne-ore procurement — when Rizhao is running hot (inferred from this series strength), it competes aggressively for Brazilian and Australian iron ore cargoes at Rizhao port. Monthly output above 6.5 Mt for Shandong indicates the province's mills are at or above designed capacity; output above 7 Mt is the historical ceiling before government output restriction commentary emerges.

rics.description: Steel production, Shanghai MunicipalityCurrent Period
rics.meaning: Monthly current-period steel production in Shanghai Municipality, published by the NBS Shanghai Bureau. Shanghai (~20 Mt/year steel capacity) is anchored entirely by Baowu's Baoshan complex — the world's first purpose-built coastal integrated steel mill (opened 1985), now one of the world's most advanced steel plants, producing high-end automotive steel, electrical steel, and shipbuilding plate. Shanghai is a benchmark for China's premium steel quality capabilities.
rics.how_to_use: Shanghai/Baoshan is China's premium flat steel indicator — when this series rises, it signals healthy demand in auto (SAIC, local JV production), shipbuilding (Jiangnan Shipyard), and appliance sectors that consume Baoshan's high-value grades (dual-phase, ultra-high-strength, grain-oriented electrical steel). A divergence where Shanghai flat steel output rises while small/medium section production (aCNPDMNSST) falls confirms the steel sector is operating on an industrial/consumer rather than property demand cycle.
